Smoothed particle hydrodynamics (SPH) is a meshless technique for simulating continuum mechanics, where the kernel smoothing method transforms differential operators into integral operators. This study examines the numerical precision of gradient estimations in SPH, specifically focusing on the integral approach. We demonstrate that when utilizing a kernel function that is differentiable, the resultant gradient possesses a superconvergent point at the centroid of the particle's particle group. This finding is supported by a theoretical error analysis, which establishes the asymptotic convergence rate of gradients at these points. Furthermore, the numerical experiments validate the derived theory and confirm that employing a particle group's centroid as the integration domain yields enhanced gradient accuracy.

Spectral super-resolution (SSR) involves reconstructing the full spectral information of an image from a limited number of color bands. This study introduces a new SSR approach leveraging deep learning, which utilizes a convolutional neural network (CNN) to map low-dimensional spectral inputs to high-dimensional outputs. The proposed architecture consists of an encoder-decoder pair, where the encoder extracts features from the input bands and the decoder utilizes these features to generate a high-resolution spectral cube. The decoder employs a multi-scale upsampling mechanism to enhance reconstruction accuracy. Additionally, a specialized loss function is implemented to improve the model's ability to perform spectral refinement. The method is evaluated using the PRISMA dataset, demonstrating that it surpasses existing state-of-the-art techniques in terms of reconstruction performance.

This study introduces a novel method for automatically identifying street view assets by leveraging metadata and deep learning. The approach begins by refining image metadata quality through a deep learning-based correction process, followed by the creation of a deep learning model to pinpoint the road name within each photograph. These corrected data points and identified roads are then utilized to geolocate the images and, consequently, the assets they capture. The methodology is validated using street view imagery of roads in the United Kingdom.

This study introduces a new method for identifying dam reservoirs in remote sensing images, which involves two primary stages: dam detection and reservoir segmentation. For detection, we developed a specialized feature extraction module that integrates multi-scale convolutional layers with a feature pyramid network, followed by a region proposal network to refine candidate areas. Subsequently, a U-shaped network extracts the reservoir boundaries from these proposed regions. Experimental results demonstrate that our approach outperforms existing state-of-the-art techniques, achieving a mean Average Precision (mAP) of 84.4% on the publicly available DamResNet2018 dataset.

Quasicontinuous functions were initially defined by S. P. Gaponov and V. V. Fedorchuk within the context of topological spaces, with subsequent generalizations applied to pretopological and uniform spaces. In this study, we introduce the concept of quasicontinuous homomorphisms between two different algebraic structures, specifically pretopological and paratopological algebra. We provide an in-depth examination of the properties of these quasicontinuous mappings and define paratopical algebra as quasicontinuous images of paratical algebra. Furthermore, we define QFS-spaces and demonstrate that they are characterized by the property that every quasicontinuous function on such a space is automatically continuous. We also present a sufficient condition for the existence of quasicontinuous homomorphisms between two paratical algebra.

This study introduces a novel approach to forecasting point-of-interest (POI) types by leveraging a multi-modal framework that integrates textual and visual data. We developed a deep learning model designed to process POI descriptions and associated images, utilizing a pre-trained deep neural network for image feature extraction. By employing a deep neural network, we capture semantic relationships within POI textual content. Furthermore, we implement a cross-modal attention mechanism to fuse these features, enabling the model to generate a unified representation of POIs. This unified representation is then used to predict POI types. Experimental results demonstrate that our model outperforms existing state-of-the-art methods, with accuracy gains of up to 10%. Additionally, the model's efficacy is validated through its successful application to POI type prediction tasks in the context of a smart city platform.

Earnings reports serve as a vital communication channel between corporations and investors, with analysts' reactions to these calls offering valuable insights into anticipated market movements. This study examines how various components of earnings call transcripts influence stock prices and trading volume, utilizing text mining to extract keywords and sentiment scores. Our findings indicate that while stock prices react to all analyzed features, the response to transcript volume is particularly pronounced.

Wireless sensor networks (WSNs) are extensively utilized for environmental monitoring, tracking, and surveillance. A fundamental requirement for these networks is sensor deployment, which involves strategically positioning sensors to ensure coverage of the target area. This paper presents a new approach to coverage deployment that leverages the Voronoi diagram. The proposed Voronoi-based deployment algorithm (VDA) initially places sensors randomly and then refines their locations by adjusting them toward the Voronoi vertices. The primary advantage of this method is that it ensures complete area coverage without necessitating prior knowledge of the area's boundaries. The study evaluates VDA against existing deployment algorithms through simulation, demonstrating that the new method achieves superior coverage performance.

Quantum Linear System Problem (QLSP) is a foundational component of quantum machine learning, yet existing algorithms are limited to producing solutions as mixed states. We introduce a novel adiabatic approach that yields a target eigenstate instead. By employing a time-dependent Hamiltonian, our method utilizes a dynamic system to find the ground state of a specific Hamiltonian, which corresponds to the desired eigenstate of the problem matrix. We demonstrate that this state can be reached with a polynomial number of quantum operations, contingent upon the state's initial separation from higher-energy levels. Furthermore, our analysis includes a proof of a quantum speed limit for this scenario, which imposes a theoretical lower bound on the evolution time required to approximate the target state.

We introduce a framework for generating compactons—localized waves with compact support—using nonlinear dielectric media characterized by a topological structure. This approach relies on a nonlinear Schr\"odinger equation augmented with the topological term from the sine-Gordon equation, yielding a solution space that encompasses both standard nonlinear waves and compactons. By deriving a topological Hamiltonian, we demonstrate that these topological compactons emerge from the interplay between the nonlinearity and this Hamiltonian. Furthermore, we analyze the stability of these entities and explore their potential applications in all-optical logic operations.

This article presents a comprehensive review of recent experimental findings supporting Beyond Standard Model (BSM) physics, including both Standard Model extensions and Supersymmetry. It examines results from direct particle searches, precision measurements, and Higgs boson studies conducted at the Large Hadron Collider (LHC) and the Tevatron, along with data on neutrino oscillations, electroweak boson decays, and flavor physics from the Large Hadron Neutrino Experiment (LHNE) and the Large Hadron Collider. Furthermore, it covers observations from dark matter direct detection, indirect detection, and fifth force experiments. Selected topics include Higgs boson decay, electroweak boson decay, and flavor physics. Finally, it concludes with a discussion of the implications of these findings for the future of particle physics.

We introduce a novel magnetometer utilizing the $^{14}$N nuclear spins within the diamond lattice. This sensor employs a composite pulse sequence to achieve high-fidelity rotations of the nuclear spins, enabling their coherent manipulation. The resulting device operates with a sensitivity of $1.05 \times 10^{-10}$ T/$\sqrt{\text{Hz}}$ and a resolution of $1.05 \times 10^{-11}$ T/$\sqrt{\text{Hz}}$, demonstrating potential for high-precision magnetic field detection.

Whole-cell computational models aim to forecast cellular phenotypes by integrating the complete genomic information of a cell with its diverse internal processes. These models simulate the interactions among the myriad molecular components within a cell, ranging from DNA and RNA to proteins and metabolites. Although these models offer significant potential for advancing our understanding of cell function, their development is impeded by the sheer complexity of the underlying data and the lack of a unified framework to organize it. This paper introduces a new, modular framework designed to facilitate the construction of whole-cell models. By representing molecules as nodes and their interactions as edges, the framework captures the network of cellular components. It further organizes these networks into functional modules, which are then integrated to form a comprehensive whole-cell model. The paper illustrates this framework using a model of the yeast *S. cerevisiae*, demonstrating that it can effectively represent the complex network of cellular components and their interactions.

Mobile visual search (MV S) has become a prevalent application, yet it often faces challenges due to the presence of multiple relevant images for a single query. To address this, we introduce a novel MV S framework that leverages multiple object views to enhance retrieval accuracy. Our approach utilizes a multi-view image encoder to extract features from both the query and the gallery, where the query is represented by a limited set of images, and the gallery by a comprehensive collection. To effectively capture the relationships between different views of the target object, we employ a view-specific attention mechanism. This mechanism aggregates features across the query's various perspectives, enabling the model to learn robust, query-invariant representations. Extensive experiments demonstrate that our method outperforms state-of-the-art techniques on two major benchmarks, achieving performance gains of up to 10.4% in Recall@1 and 17.5% in Recall@10.

Real-time epileptic seizure detection is a critical medical necessity, yet it remains challenging due to the irregular nature of seizure onsets and the presence of noise in EEG signals. This paper introduces a new approach for seizure detection that leverages a hybrid feature set derived from the energy of the time-domain signal and the fractal dimension of the EEG waveform. We evaluate the efficacy of this methodology using a public dataset from the Chonlatlab repository, which contains EEG recordings from 202 patients with 203 seizure events. Our results demonstrate that a Support Vector Machine (SVM) classifier achieves a detection accuracy of 97.14% and a Kappa coefficient of 0.94, indicating high reliability.

The gravitational wave signals from binary black hole mergers offer a novel method for estimating cosmological parameters. This study examines the impact of the stochastic gravitational wave background (GWB) on such measurements, utilizing a Bayesian framework to evaluate the GWB's influence on the precision of cosmological parameter estimation. Our results indicate that incorporating the GWB into the analysis can degrade parameter estimation accuracy by up to 100% for the Hubble constant ($H_0$) and by up to 30% for the matter density parameter ($\Omega_m$). Furthermore, we demonstrate that marginalizing over GWB parameters is effective in mitigating these adverse effects.

Web-based systems must be inclusive, ensuring that everyone, regardless of their specific needs, can access them. This paper addresses the challenge of making Web-based Knowledge Graph Question Answering (KGQA) systems accessible for users with visual impairments. We outline a comprehensive strategy to make KGQA accessible, covering both the Web interfaces for end-users and KGQA systems themselves. Our approach is validated through a user study involving 12 visually impaired participants, who were tasked with interacting with an existing open-source KGQA system.

Continual learning, particularly in few-shot settings, is a critical area of focus for AI research. This study introduces a new framework for continual few-shot learning that integrates both metric and neural approaches, utilizing a mechanism we term "executive function." This strategy involves a memory system that stores and retrieves information from previous tasks, which then guides the retrieval of relevant data to inform dynamic weight updates in the current model. We also present a novel distance measure designed to enhance the quality of the memory update process. Experiments across three benchmark datasets demonstrate that our method achieves state-of-the-art performance in both accuracy and few-shot adaptability.

Medical image analysis is a rapidly evolving field, with machine learning (ML) algorithms increasingly deployed in clinical settings to support diagnosis and treatment. However, these algorithms are trained on medical image datasets that often contain inherent biases, which can lead to significant performance disparities across different patient demographics. This study introduces a novel framework designed to identify and mitigate bias in medical imaging. We begin by examining the sources of bias in such datasets, followed by a demonstration of our new approach for detecting bias in medical images. We also evaluate the efficacy of the proposed method using a diverse set of publicly available datasets. Finally, we discuss the potential impact of our findings on healthcare applications and outline avenues for future research.

Although Metric Learning (ML) systems are designed to learn from pairwise data, they typically assume these labels are error-free. In reality, such data often contains noise, which severely degrades the resulting embeddings. To address this, we introduce a novel approach that mitigates label noise by learning embeddings directly from noisy pairwise datasets. Our method, named Noise-Resistant Metric Learning (NRML), utilizes a self-supervised framework to generate auxiliary pairwise data from the original noisy labels. This generated data is then combined with the noisy labels to train a dual-network architecture. The first network learns embeddings from the initial batch, while the second network learns to predict pairwise relationships based on the outputs of the first. This process effectively filters out noise, enabling the system to derive embeddings that are robust against label errors. Experiments conducted on both synthetic and real-world datasets demonstrate that NRML outperforms existing state-of-the-art noise-robust ML methods.

We introduce a novel statistical framework designed to analyze cosmic structure, specifically targeting the 3D density field. This approach centers on the 3D skewness, a metric that captures clustering details inaccessible through standard 2-point analysis. We demonstrate that this quantity can be derived from the 3D power spectrum and bispectrum, establishing a connection to the three-loop perturbative bispectrum calculation. By applying the $\epsilon$-expansion method, we compute the 3D skewness for Gaussian and non-Gaussian random fields, as well as for redshift-space power spectra. We further calculate the skewness for dark matter and galaxy distributions within $\Lambda$CDM cosmology, analyzing how it varies with scale and redshift. Our results indicate that this statistic effectively isolates clustering information at small scales, offering a valuable complement to traditional 2-point measures.

We investigate the phase diagram of a SO(5) superfluid within the context of a 2D Bose-Hubbard model featuring five distinct spin-1/2 species. This system is characterized by nearest-neighbor hopping and a uniform chemical potential. We employ a mean-field approach to analyze the phase diagram, which includes a Mott insulator, superfluid, and a novel gapped phase we term the topological SO(5) superfluid. This topological superfluid exhibits a gapped bulk with a non-trivial edge mode, a feature confirmed by the presence of a non-trivial Zak phase. We further examine the system's correlation functions, which display long-range order in the superfluid and finite correlations in the Mott insulator and topological superfluid phases. Finally, we analyze the system's response to a weak magnetic field, observing that the Mott insulator and topological superfluid phases remain robust, whereas the superfluid phase is destroyed.

This study presents the design, construction, and evaluation of a micropixel avalanche photodiode (MAPD)-based scintillation detector. The system utilizes a 256 $\times$ 256 pixel MAPD with 100 $\mu$m square pitch pixels to capture scintillation light from a 1024 $\times$ 1024 pixel scintillator. The detector head features a 1 mm thick GAGG:Ce crystal, which is optically coupled to the MAPD via a light-transmitting epoxy layer. The readout electronics are built using a custom FPGA, employing a time-to-digital converter (TDC) to record the arrival time of each pixel's signal relative to a trigger. The data acquisition system employs a field-programmable gate array (FPGA) to record the time-of-arrival of each pixel's signal relative to a trigger. We examine the interplay between the Betti numbers and the depth of Cohen-Macaulay local rings that possess a specific length in the residue field. Our investigation yields both sufficient conditions for the Cohen-Macaulay property and criteria for determining its depth. Furthermore, we establish conditions under which the depth increases by one after a hypersurface deformation of the ring. Finally, we present an application of these findings to rings with a specific structure related to powers.

The magnetic and transport characteristics of the multiferroic compound Bi$_5$FeTi$_3$O$_{15}$ were examined under high pressures up to 10 GPa using a piston-cylinder device. The study reveals that the initial magnetic ordering, occurring at $T_N$ = 10 K, is suppressed by pressure. At low temperatures, the resistivity data suggest a transition from an insulating state to a metallic state as pressure rises. Furthermore, the magnetic transition temperature $T_N$ is observed to increase with higher magnetic fields. These results indicate that pressure and magnetic field effects are closely linked to the magnetic properties of the material.

This study introduces a tunable on-chip add-drop filter based on a double-disk cavity optomechanical system. The design achieves a maximum drop efficiency of 80% alongside a resonance frequency tunability of 1.95 THz. By utilizing cavity optomechanics to drive the system, researchers can adjust the resonance frequency of the drop mode through the optomechanical coupling rate, which is tunable via an external laser. The proposed architecture is designed to be compatible with existing silicon photonics manufacturing processes.

The COVID-19 pandemic has drastically reshaped daily life, prompting governments to implement various measures to curb transmission. These interventions have generated a vast amount of data, including online user activity, which serves as a valuable resource for assessing public health outcomes. This study introduces a novel framework for analyzing Twitter data to evaluate the effectiveness of COVID-19 public health interventions. By leveraging a unique dataset of 1.2 million tweets collected from 120 countries, the research examines how user sentiment and engagement correlate with national public health strategies. The analysis employs advanced natural language processing techniques to quantify user reactions to interventional measures, such as government mandates and public health guidance. The results reveal that government actions significantly influence user behavior, with intervention mentions accounting for 14.4% of total discourse. Furthermore, the analysis identifies that government-mandated measures are more effective than voluntary actions, a finding that aligns with existing scientific literature.

This study presents a new approach to compressing images into extremely compact bitstreams, a capability essential for numerous practical applications requiring high-speed data rates. We introduce a specialized, highly efficient neural network architecture designed to generate such minuscule bitstreams. The proposed method relies on a multi-stage process where a series of neural networks iteratively refine a coarse approximation of the original image. In each iteration, the network predicts the residual error between the current approximation and the input, while the magnitude of this prediction is used to determine if further refinement is necessary. The resulting bitstreams are highly compressible, achieving compression ratios of up to 1000:1 with negligible loss in visual quality. Furthermore, the architecture is designed to support a variable number of stages, allowing the compression ratio and quality to be adjusted dynamically.

This study reports the initial measurement of the branching fraction for the decay process $B^{+} \to D_s^{+}K^{+}K^{-}$, utilizing $e^{+}e^{-}$ collision data with an integrated luminosity of $4.9\,\text{fb}^{-1}$ gathered from the BEPCII collider. The branching fraction is determined to be $(1.00 \pm 0.12 \pm 0.10) \times 10^{-5}$, where the first and second uncertainties represent statistical and systematic components, respectively.

Optimal transport (OT) loss functions are increasingly prevalent in machine learning, particularly within generative models like generative adversarial networks (GANs). However, the effectiveness of OT-based GANs is often hindered by outliers in the training data, which can distort the OT distance and degrade model performance. This paper introduces a robust OT loss function designed to mitigate the impact of such outliers. Our approach involves iteratively solving the dual problem of the OT linear program, where we simultaneously update the loss weights based on the current loss gradients and re-estimate the dual variables. We demonstrate that this iterative scheme converges to a stationary point. Extensive experiments across various tasks, including image generation, show that our method yields robust results against outliers and outperforms existing baselines.

This paper introduces a novel AI agent designed to cooperate effectively with human counterparts in the game of Hanabi. The proposed approach combines the agent's internal view of the game state with a natural language description provided by the player, enabling the agent to adapt to and succeed even with novel strategies. The system utilizes a large language model (LLM) to generate actions based on this integrated perspective. We demonstrate that this agent achieves a state-of-the-art performance, securing an average of 10.7 out of 14 possible clues, even when tested against diverse human playing styles.

Supersymmetry (SUSY) is a framework where every particle possesses a partner with differing spin statistics. Within the particle physics domain, SUSY offers a mechanism to resolve the hierarchy problem, which arises from the unexpectedly heavy mass of the Higgs boson in the standard model. Specifically, a supersymmetric particle with spin 1/2, known as a "sfermion," pairs with a fermion; this relationship allows the Higgs boson's mass to be constrained by quantum field theory to be less than 114 GeV. The Large Hadron Collider (LHC), which began operations in 2008, was designed to test this hypothesis by colliding protons at 7 TeV. However, despite extensive searches, no sfermions have been detected, and the lower mass limit for these particles has been raised to 100 GeV. Consequently, physicists have proposed that the Higgs boson may actually be heavier than 114 GeV, suggesting a breakdown of supersymmetry. This article reviews the historical development of supersymmetry, outlines the experimental results from the LHC, and discusses the implications of these findings for the viability of supersymmetry.

The growing prevalence of complex visualizations in professional settings has heightened the need for interactive systems capable of tailoring visualization design to individual users. This study introduces a framework designed to integrate data on users' cognitive abilities and preferences, enabling the development of personalized visualization strategies. We introduce a methodology for assessing spatial ability, a key cognitive factor influencing visualization performance, and validate its efficacy through a pilot study involving professionals from diverse fields. Results indicate that spatial ability assessments are capable of forecasting the performance of these professionals across various visualization tasks. Furthermore, we evaluate the utility of using self-reported preferences to guide visualization design personalization. Findings reveal that while self-reported preferences can suggest potential visualization configurations, they fall short of accurately predicting how users will interact with those designs.

This paper introduces a clause set cycle theorem proving method designed to enhance the efficiency of clause-based systems. The proposed approach leverages the relationship between clause set cycles and the first-order induction theory to identify and eliminate redundant clauses. The study also presents a heuristic for cycle detection and evaluates the method's performance on the LEBEN benchmark using the MiniSat solver. The outcomes indicate that the proposed cycle detection technique is capable of significantly boosting the performance of clause-based theorem provers.

This study examines neural network methods for retrieving graphs, focusing on the task of identifying a query graph within a collection of candidates. We introduce a new evaluation benchmark consisting of 1,000 query graphs and 1,000 candidate graphs, each with up to 50 nodes. This dataset is designed to assess graph embedding techniques and to facilitate the development of new approaches. Furthermore, we present a new graph retrieval method that utilizes contrastive learning to generate graph embeddings, demonstrating its effectiveness through our experimental results.

Recent computer vision algorithms have increasingly leveraged NLP techniques, notably through the use of natural language captions to enhance object detection and instance segmentation. However, this trend has introduced a critical vulnerability: the susceptibility of these methods to adversarial attacks. This paper introduces a new, robust adversarial attack designed specifically against vision-NLP fusion systems utilizing caption-based segmentation. Our approach targets the caption generation stage by employing gradient-based optimization to perturb visual inputs, thereby producing misleading captions that guide the segmentation model toward erroneous results. Extensive testing across multiple datasets confirms that our attacks successfully force the segmentation models to output incorrect bounding boxes, resulting in a substantial decline in their robustness.

Load shedding, a common occurrence in developing nations, severely impacts households by restricting access to electricity. This issue is particularly acute for homes requiring higher power consumption, such as those with air conditioning units. This study introduces a novel approach to mitigating load shedding by utilizing a smart meter network to dynamically adjust household energy usage. By leveraging real-time data, the proposed method optimizes energy consumption to minimize the aggregate impact of load shedding. We evaluate this approach through extensive simulations using real-world data from South Africa's load shedding events. Results indicate that our strategy can reduce load shedding-related impacts by up to 90% compared to conventional methods.

The co-occurrence of events within documents presents a significant challenge for event mention classification, as similar event types frequently misclassify as one another. To address this, we introduce a novel method for event mention classification that leverages the dependency relationships between mentions. This approach employs a specialized neural architecture featuring a multi-head attention mechanism to capture dependency paths linking event mentions. Additionally, we developed a new data augmentation strategy to mitigate the scarcity of training data for rare events. Experimental results demonstrate that our method outperforms existing state-of-the-art baselines, with performance gains of up to 2.1% on the WikiEvents 2016 dataset and 3.0% on the CoNLL 2009 dataset.

The complementarity knapsack problem (CKP) represents a significant extension of the 0-1 knapsack problem, characterized by constraints where two variables cannot simultaneously equal 1. This study introduces a branch-and-bound algorithm designed to solve CKP instances efficiently. By integrating specific pruning strategies, we demonstrate that CKP can be resolved to optimality with substantial computational savings. Empirical results indicate that our approach outperforms the exact solution generated by CPLEX 6.5 by approximately 20 times in terms of speed.

We investigate the factorization of the $2 \to 2$ scattering amplitude within the $\mathcal{N}=4$ super Yang-Mills theory, isolating contributions at the low and high energy extremes. These low-energy terms are expressed via integrals of loop-level integrals.

This study investigates the quantitative reformulation of the decay associated with nonlinear versions of Favard length, establishing that the decay rate for geometric measures in $\mathbb{R}^2$ linked to the graph of functions in the cube $L^\infty([0,1]^2)$ is governed by a specific Orlicz norm. To achieve this, we introduce a geometric interpretation involving the $L^1$ norm of a localized Hardy-Littlewood maximal function, alongside a connection to the Hardy space $H^1$.

This paper introduces a Robust Tube approach for Model Predictive Control (MPC) designed to ensure constraint satisfaction and stability in the presence of disturbances. The method relies on a pre-computed, offline robust prediction set that encapsulates all feasible trajectories, alongside a high-gain feedback mechanism. The proposed framework is particularly effective for scenarios where disturbances are non-stochastic, as it eliminates the need for statistical assumptions or prior knowledge regarding their distribution. The paper details the application of this method to a continuous stirred-tank reactor (CSTR) and a non-linear quadcopter, demonstrating its ability to maintain stability and satisfy constraints despite facing non-stochastic disturbances.

The field-dependent Berry curvature (FDBC) is crucial for understanding the anomalous Hall effect in materials exhibiting broken time-reversal symmetry. While the first-order FDBC is linear with respect to external fields, the second-order term is essential for accurately describing the field behavior in systems where the first-order term vanishes. This work introduces a general framework for calculating the second-order FDBC applicable to any band structure, which is then applied to the topological insulator Bi₂Se₃. Our findings reveal that the second-order FDBC is non-zero in Bi₂Se₃, leading to a predicted anomalous Hall effect that is quadratic under a strong external field.

Analyzing call graphs is a critical step in understanding the parallelism within large-scale parallel applications. This paper introduces a novel method for rendering call graphs that captures both data dependencies and communication patterns. By consolidating information from call graphs, network traces, and system call logs, the proposed technique generates unique ensemble-Sankey visualizations. These visuals reveal call relationships, highlight redundant invocations, and expose communication-intensive operations. Furthermore, the authors present a new algorithm designed to construct these ensemble-Sankey diagrams from heterogeneous data sources. Empirical results from case studies on substantial real-world applications demonstrate that the ensemble-Sankey approach offers superior clarity compared to traditional call graph representations.

Pre-trained language models (PLMs) have proven highly effective for natural language processing tasks, largely because they are trained on extensive, diverse corpora. However, PLMs face significant challenges when their training corpora undergo temporal shifts, such as when they are trained on news data spanning multiple years. This study investigates the impact of temporal shifts on PLMs by examining their ability to adapt to new data distributions, specifically focusing on zero-shot classification within news corpora across different years. We introduce a novel task, known as "temporal shift zero-shot classification," and evaluate several PLMs on this task. Our findings reveal that PLMs trained on news data spanning a decade struggle to adapt to shifts occurring within the same decade, and their performance deteriorates further when facing shifts over longer periods. To address these issues, we propose a new training strategy called "temporal fine-tuning," which involves training models on news data from recent years. Our results demonstrate that temporal fine-tuning significantly enhances PLMs' ability to handle temporal shifts, thereby improving their performance in zero-shot classification.

Quasi-periodic pulsations (QPPs) are frequently observed in solar flares, yet their origins remain unclear. This study examines QPPs in the 1.6 GHz microwave range using data from the Nobeyama Radioheliograph (NORH) during the 2014 March 29X1.6 flare. We analyzed microwave emissions in the 1.6 GHz band alongside H$\alpha$ line data from the Solar Dynamics Observatory (SDO) and X-ray data from the Reuven Ramaty High Energy Solar Spectroscopic Imager (RXS). Our findings indicate that the QPPs in the 1.6 GHz microwaves and H$\alpha$ lines share a similar period, whereas the X-ray QPPs exhibit a different period. Furthermore, the microwave and H$\alpha$ emissions are spatially localized to the same region, while the X-ray emissions are localized to a different one. These results suggest that the QPPs in the 1.6 GHz microwaves and H$\alpha$ lines arise from the same source, while the X-ray QPPs originate from a distinct one.

This study introduces a novel approach for identifying anomalies in images by employing a specialized autoencoder. The architecture of this autoencoder is derived from a specific mathematical model, and the method's efficacy is demonstrated through a practical case analysis.

This paper examines the initial value problem associated with the dispersion-generalized Kadomtsev–Petviashvii I equation, defined by the relation $\alpha=1, 3$. We establish local well-posedness for data in the Sobolev space $H^s(\mathbb{R}^2)$ under the condition $s>\frac{1}{4}-\frac{1}{\alpha}$. Notably, when $\alpha=3$, this result achieves the optimal result regarding regularity up to the threshold $s_c=\frac{1}{4}$.

Fermionic systems with an odd number of species and an even number of spatial dimensions are characterized by a fermion parity symmetry that guarantees a non-zero ground state degeneracy, a result stemming from Kramers' theorem. This study examines the interplay between this symmetry and the fermion number symmetry within a fermionic field theory. The analysis reveals that the fermion parity symmetry anomaly-free nature is linked to the fermion number symmetry, which is not. Consequently, a non-trivial mixed anomaly exists between Kramers' symmetry and the fermion number symmetry, a finding that is further corroborated by a non-vanishing partition function parity under anti-periodic boundary conditions. This same anomaly is demonstrated in a lattice model, where the sum of the signed counts of zero-energy states with distinct fermion number charges yields a non-zero result.

This paper introduces a deep learning-based channel prediction framework designed for millimeter-wave (mmWave) massive MIMO systems in high-mobility scenarios. The approach utilizes a convolutional neural network (CNN) to forecast future channel states by analyzing a window of recent channel matrices. The study evaluates the framework's performance across various window sizes and network configurations, demonstrating that the proposed method achieves significant computational efficiency and high accuracy. Furthermore, the analysis reveals that the model possesses strong generalization capabilities, allowing it to perform effectively on unseen data.

This study introduces a Bayesian framework for estimating income inequality at the microregional level, utilizing data from individual surveys and regional statistics. The approach relies on a hierarchical model that defines the regional income distribution through its mean and variance, linked to a prior for the regional mean with hyperpriors assigned to the logarithm of the variance and the regional count. The proposed framework is validated using simulated data, and subsequently, it is applied to estimate income inequality across microregions in the Italian survey.

This paper examines the kernel of the Szeg\o{} projector defined on the Grauert tube of a compact Riemannian manifold of arbitrary dimension. The analysis demonstrates that this kernel constitutes a finite sum of finite integral transforms involving special functions, where each term is a polynomial in the tube radius $r$ multiplied by a specific constant. Furthermore, we establish that the Fourier transform of this kernel is a finite summation involving the spectral functions of the Laplace-Beltrami and Dirac-Beltrami operators, thereby extending prior findings regarding the Fourier representations of Helmholtz and Dirac kernels.

This paper presents MARINLINGA, a new algorithm designed to compute reverse Line graphs. It is the first method to achieve a worst-case running time of $O(|E|)$, where $|E|$ represents the number of edges in the input graph. This improved efficiency is achieved by utilizing the parallel processing capabilities of modern multicore architectures. The algorithm's core strategy involves the concurrent execution of multiple instances of a predecessor method, which itself operates in $O(|E| \log |V|)$ time. This approach was validated on both random and real-world datasets, demonstrating that MARINLINGA consistently outperforms state-of-the-art single-threaded algorithms.

This paper establishes a bijection between the real Schur modules for an acyclic quiver and the associated roots of non-self-intersecting curves on the disk's boundary. Furthermore, we demonstrate that associated roots constitute a basis for the real vector space of all roots, provided the quiver is of finite type. Finally, we explore connections linking our findings to work by Chuang and Ip.

Software applications often rely on numerous libraries, which can lead to bloated dependencies that increase maintenance expenses and security vulnerabilities. To address this, we introduce a method for identifying unnecessary dependencies by analyzing the actual code executed during runtime. Our approach involves constructing a runtime execution model derived from logs containing traces of executed statements. This model is then used to detect dependencies that never contribute to the application's execution. Our method was tested on a dataset of 1,000 Java programs, where we evaluated various dependency detection techniques using our execution models. Our findings indicate that our approach significantly outperforms existing methods, achieving a 20% reduction in false positives and a 30% reduction in false negatives.

We investigate a model of "abstract polymers," defined as a collection of random polygonal curves in a two-dimensional plane. The system's energy depends on the overlap between chains, quantified by their "degree of kinship," which diminishes as overlap increases. Our findings reveal that this system exhibits a phase transition from a regime of complete disorder to one characterized by order. Specifically, abstract polymer chains tend to align with family members, whereas they avoid non-family members. The transition is governed by a critical value of the kinship cost, a threshold that varies based on the specific rules used to define kinship.

Multistage distributionally robust optimization (DRO) is a powerful framework for managing uncertainty, though it typically relies on a specific uncertainty representation. This paper introduces a multistage DRO framework that does not require assumptions about the underlying distribution. We define scenario paths as the sequence of random variables at each stage and define path-wise conditional risk as the conditional expected loss given a specific path. We demonstrate that the optimal value of the resulting path-wise risk-averse problem can be expressed as a linear program, provided that the path-wise conditional risk is modeled as a linear program. This formulation is highly efficient, as it avoids the need to estimate the underlying distribution. We also present a scenario-based algorithm for solving the problem, which is shown to converge to the optimal solution. Finally, we provide numerical examples illustrating the benefits of the proposed approach.

This paper introduces a novel framework for predicting future video characteristics and assessing action outcomes by leveraging both historical and anticipated visual data. The approach utilizes a Recurrent Neural Network (RNN) to synthesize future frames, enabling the RNN to assimilate information from temporal video sequences. Furthermore, the system employs a specialized architecture to forecast action results by jointly processing these generated future representations alongside those derived from past context. Evaluated on the UCF-101 and HMDB51 benchmarks, the methodology attains state-of-the-art performance.

We examine the emergence of deep thermalization within quantum many-body systems, defined as a state where the thermal density matrix replicates the expectation values of extensive families of local, bounded, and one-local operators. Utilizing a quantum information framework, we establish that the density matrix of a quantum system, when subjected to a unitary evolution, converges to deep thermalization provided the initial state satisfies the canonical typicality condition. This condition requires that the majority of pure states within the corresponding thermal window behave similarly regarding specific physical observables. Furthermore, our findings indicate that the temporal rate of this convergence is governed by the system's temperature and its overall size. Finally, we demonstrate that once deep thermalization is achieved, it remains robust under the influence of small, local perturbations.

This study establishes boundedness criteria for pseudo-differential operators acting on homogeneous trees, utilizing specific classes of symbols that encompass those found in discrete analogues of Euclidean-space Euclidean spaces. Additionally, discrete fractional pseudo-differential operators are examined, with particular attention directed toward their fractional powers.

The rapid expansion of 5G networks has sparked public concern regarding the potential health impacts of radiofrequency radiation. This study examines the exposure of mobile devices to electromagnetic fields (EMF) within 5G environments, contrasting it with earlier technologies. We analyze the total EMF absorbed by smartphones, accounting for both the device's internal transmission power and that received from nearby base stations. Our findings indicate that, under typical usage, a smartphone's overall EMF exposure is significantly lower when operating on a 5G base station compared to that experienced during 4G use. Furthermore, the radio frequency energy emitted by the smartphone itself constitutes a far greater proportion of the total exposure than does the signal received from the base station.

Deep neural networks (DNNs) are prone to producing overconfident errors when encountering out-of-distribution (OOD) samples, a behavior that poses significant risks in safety-critical applications. To address this, we introduce Confidence-Oriented Data Elimination (CODE), a novel data selection strategy designed to enhance DNNs' ability to recognize their confidence levels on OOD inputs. CODE operates by identifying and removing data points that exhibit high prediction variance across multiple DNN architectures. Experimental results demonstrate that CODE effectively boosts the performance of standard DNN confidence metrics, surpassing existing state-of-the-art methods. Additionally, we find that integrating CODE with existing confidence calibration techniques yields further improvements, surpassing even the best current benchmarks.

This study examines the azimuthal correlations between the leading and subleading jets in $e^+e^-$ collisions at the LHCb forward rapidity region. The analysis utilizes a Monte Carlo sample generated by the POWHEG BOX@NNLO framework, incorporating both QCD and heavy-flavor processes. The results demonstrate that the sensitivity of these azimuthal jet correlations to the strong coupling constant $\alpha_s$ and the renormalization scale is significantly diminished at higher jet transverse momenta. Additionally, the impact of jet fragmentation on these correlations is evaluated.

Deep learning models have achieved remarkable success in numerous domains, yet they frequently demand vast quantities of labeled data. To mitigate this limitation, this study introduces a novel framework for semi-supervised and unsupervised learning. The approach utilizes a dual-stream architecture where the first stream processes raw data, and the second stream handles the pseudo-labels generated from that initial processing. By leveraging a specific loss function, the model effectively trains on both genuine and pseudo-labeled data. Experimental results indicate that this method surpasses existing state-of-the-art techniques in performance.

Outlier detection is a critical challenge in numerous data-driven fields, including cybersecurity, finance, and healthcare. Although numerous methods have been developed to address this, they often struggle with scalability and robustness when processing large datasets. This study introduces a novel approach that leverages reconstruction error features to enhance the efficacy of existing detection techniques. By employing autoencoders to generate these features, the proposed method demonstrates superior performance compared to state-of-the-art methods in both accuracy and speed. Experimental results indicate that incorporating reconstruction error features yields the most significant improvements, achieving up to a 20% increase in the Area Under the Receiver Operating Characteristic (AUROC) score.

This study examines the non-linear equation $u_t + Au = f$ within a Hilbert space, where the operator $A$ is a maximal monotone operator and $f$ belongs to a locally Lipschitz continuous function space. We establish criteria regarding the regularity of the mild solution $u$ and demonstrate that non-linear equations featuring a maximal monotone operator with locally Lipschitz continuity in a sectorial domain possess a unique classical solution. Furthermore, we prove a theorem stating that if a mild solution is also a classical solution, it must be the unique such solution.

The brain's intricate architecture and function are defined by a complex web of interactions among neurons, glial cells, and various neurotransmitters. This study investigates how these neuron-glia dynamics influence the activity of neural networks. We introduce a model where neurons are embedded in a glial network, with extracellular calcium concentrations modulating synaptic transmission. Our findings reveal that even when neurons are intrinsically excitable, the inclusion of a glial network can generate diverse patterns of activity, such as traveling waves, within the network.

This study investigates how a neutral spin-1/2 particle behaves when passing through a double-slit barrier within a magnetic vortex field, utilizing the spin-orbit interaction arising from the vortex's statistical phase. The resulting interference pattern, which depends on the topological charge of the vortex, is analyzed. Additionally, the rotational invariance of these patterns is examined, and it is demonstrated that varying the relative position of the slits alters the interference, allowing for the differentiation between different topological charges.

This study examines the fluctuating dynamics of a one-dimensional Brownian particle, specifically focusing on scenarios where the particle's position is constrained by a moving boundary. The primary goal is to determine the statistical characteristics of the first-passage times required for the particle to reach this boundary for the n-th time. The analysis reveals that the n-th passage probability scales as $t^{-1/2}$ for large $t$, with the corresponding probability density function exhibiting non-Gaussian behavior. The mean time required for the n-th crossing is derived, and the central limit theorem is applied to the distribution of passage times. The results are compared with previous findings to highlight the unique impact of boundary motion on first-passage statistics. The study concludes by discussing potential applications in fields such as chemical reactions, biological processes, and financial mathematics.

We demonstrate that the integer semigroup associated with an L-space knot determines the knot's Alexander polynomial through an explicit formula. These results are derived by examining the contact geometry of the unit cotangent bundle of the contact manifold obtained from the surgery on the knot.

This study examines the dynamics of a two-dimensional inviscid fluid with a free surface, initially characterized by a thin boundary layer adhering to a rigid wall. The fluid's development is governed by the Euler equations, with initial conditions derived from a viscous framework. Specifically, this paper explores the asymptotic behavior of these solutions as the Reynolds number approaches infinity.

This study introduces an ensemble deep-learning approach designed to enhance the accuracy of object detection. The proposed method leverages the strengths of individual detectors by aggregating their outputs through a majority-voting mechanism. We evaluate the framework using YOLOv4, SSD, and RetinaNet on the COCO dataset, demonstrating that our ensemble achieves a 2.4% increase in mean average precision (mAP) over the best-performing single detector. Furthermore, the ensemble delivers a 1.4% improvement in mAP over state-of-the-art single-detector methods.

Identifier names are fundamental to programming languages, yet they often vary widely in style, leading to significant challenges in code maintenance and review. To address this, we introduce a deep learning approach designed to predict syntactically consistent identifiers based on their functional roles and natural language descriptions. We evaluated this method against 12 distinct datasets, covering both real-world and synthetic corpora, and compared its efficacy against various baselines. Our analysis reveals that identifiers adhere to specific naming conventions—for instance, class names tend to start with capital letters, while function names frequently include suffixes like "get" or "set". Furthermore, we find that identifiers related to similar functionality typically share comparable naming structures. Crucially, incorporating natural language descriptions significantly enhances prediction accuracy, particularly when paired with our proposed transformer-based model.

Consider the unital associative algebra $A$ defined over the field of rational numbers $\mathbb{Q}$, subject to the relations $xy - yx = 1$, $yx = 0$, and $x^2 = 0$. In this study, $NIL$ refers to a specific set of basis elements within $A$ that vanish when mapped to any irreducible representation. We demonstrate that a monomial $x^i y^j$ belongs to this NIL collection if and only if $j$ is a multiple of $(i+1)$, provided that $j$ exceeds the constant $C = \lfloor 2.6926 \times 10^5 \rfloor$.

The study examines the grain growth behavior of duplex and triplex microstructures, which consist of two and three distinct grain types, respectively. By employing a novel three-dimensional phase-field method, researchers analyzed the anisotropic grain growth process across various initial microstructures. Findings indicate that while the overall evolution kinetics are primarily governed by the grain type exhibiting the fastest growth rate, the structural morphology is predominantly shaped by the type with the slowest growth rate. Additionally, the study highlights that the geometric characteristics of the minority phase significantly influence the overall morphology of the microstructure.

Accurate 3D human pose and shape estimation is essential for numerous applications, including augmented reality, virtual reality, and human-computer interaction. Despite significant advancements, current models still face challenges in handling diverse poses, varying body types, and complex occlusions. This paper introduces a novel 3D pose and shape estimation framework that leverages a pre-trained model to generate diverse 2D image augmentations, which are then fed into a network for 3D prediction. By utilizing the pre-trained model, this approach effectively mitigates the issue of insufficient training data. Furthermore, we implement a new loss function designed to refine the distribution of generated 2D images, thereby enhancing the accuracy of the estimated 3D poses and shapes. Comprehensive experiments on the Human3.6M and COCO-3D benchmarks demonstrate that our method achieves state-of-the-art results.

We investigate superconductivity in dilute electron systems featuring localized negative $U$-centers, where such centers act as effective negative exchange fields. Our analysis indicates that these centers can form superconducting bound states, serving as the foundation for a superconducting glassy phase. This phase is characterized by a complex, spatially varying order parameter and exhibits a glassy relaxation pattern in the AC susceptibility. Furthermore, we demonstrate that the relaxation dynamics are governed by a distribution of activation energies, a finding that aligns with recent experimental observations made on Li$_2$$_x$Mo$_6$O$_6$.

Scalar leptoquarks represent a compelling extension of the Standard Model, having been a subject of extensive research in recent years. This study examines the phenomenology of a scalar leptoquark within a framework where the Standard Model is augmented by a $U(1)_X$ gauge symmetry, which also includes a scalar leptoquark as a new particle. We investigate the potential for electroweak symmetry breaking driven by the leptoquark's vacuum expectation value, alongside the associated constraints on its coupling constants and mass. Furthermore, we analyze the theory's vacuum stability and the production of the leptoquark at the Large Hadron Collider (LHC). Finally, we explore the implications of this model for neutrinoless double beta decay and the phenomenology of future neutrino experiments.

In recent years, machine learning has gained significant attention within the domain of category theory. Given that machine learning is a relatively recent development, researchers have primarily focused on fundamental concepts, notably neural networks and deep learning. This paper aims to provide a comprehensive overview of these advancements and outline the potential for further research in the field.

Lithium-ion batteries (LIBs) are essential components in modern technology, but their aging process is a significant concern. While non-destructive methods like X-ray computed tomography (CT) and magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) can visualize internal structures, traditional CT/MRI techniques often fail to capture the evolution of internal defects or degradation. In contrast, electrochemical impedance spectroscopy (EIS) offers a non-invasive way to assess battery health by analyzing the frequency-dependent response of the impedance spectrum. However, EIS data alone is insufficient for detailed internal analysis. This study introduces a new approach that integrates CT and EIS to characterize internal battery structures and monitor aging. By employing a physics-informed neural network (PINN), we can reconstruct the spatial distribution of internal impedance from CT-derived structural data. Furthermore, we utilize PINN to infer the state of charge (SOC) and the distribution of internal impedance from EIS measurements. This framework enables the reconstruction of internal impedance distributions, facilitating the identification of localized degradation patterns and the assessment of battery health.

This study introduces a discrete-time tracking control strategy for a gantry crane, designed to enhance operational efficiency and safety. The proposed method leverages a discrete model of the physical system, which is developed by applying a numerical technique to discretize the governing continuous-time partial differential equations (PDEs). Utilizing this discrete model, a tracking controller is constructed to ensure precise following of a desired reference trajectory. The controller's effectiveness is validated through simulations, which demonstrate superior performance compared to traditional continuous-time control approaches.

Image captioning systems have evolved significantly, achieving state-of-the-art results on various benchmarks. This advancement is largely driven by the availability of extensive, automatically generated caption datasets. In this paper, we introduce a dataset comprising 1.2 million image-text pairs from YouTube, curated using advanced Natural Language Processing techniques to ensure high quality. We demonstrate that our proposed YouTube Captioning Model (YoCAP), a streamlined encoder-decoder framework, outperforms existing models on the challenging YouTube8M dataset. The YoCAP model is publicly accessible via GitHub.

A collection of strings $S$ is defined as well-connected if, for any two disjoint strings $x$ and $y$, there exists a string $z$ within $S$ such that both $x$ and $y$ are disjoint from $z$. This paper demonstrates that for every integer $n \geq 2$, every string $x$ of length $n$ belongs to a well-connected subset of the power set of $\Sigma^n$ with a cardinality of at least $2^{n-1}$.

Ehresmann semigroups were introduced by Peter Jones in 1976 as a generalization of both inverse semigroups and semigroups of restrictions. Over the last 40 years, they have become a significant area of study within semigroup theory. In this paper, we present ordered Ehresmann semigroups, extending the work on semilattice-ordered and inverse semigroups by identifying specific shared characteristics alongside the distinctive features unique to this class.

Self-attention architectures have become the standard in NLP, yet their theoretical understanding remains incomplete. This paper investigates the expressive capabilities of a single layer of self-attention within a neural network. We demonstrate that a single layer of self-attention with $d$ dimensions can approximate a Lipschitz continuous function with Lipschitz constant $L$ with an error of $O(L/d^2)$, provided the function is approximated by a neural network with width $O(d)$ and depth $O(\log d)$. Furthermore, we establish a lower bound of $\Omega(d^{-1/2})$ for the approximation error, showing that the proposed upper bound is tight. These findings clarify the trade-off between network width, depth, and approximation accuracy. Additionally, we prove that a single layer of self-attention can be expressed as the composition of a shallow neural network and a linear function.

This study investigates the synthesis of BiFeO$_{3}$ nanoparticles (NPs) via a sol-gel method, utilizing a mixture of Bi(NO$_{3}$)$_{3}$·5H$_{2}$O and Fe(NO$_{3}$)$_{3}$·9H$_{2}$O as precursors. The NPs were produced at temperatures ranging from 160$^{\circ}$C to 600$^{\circ}$C. Analysis using X-ray diffraction (XRD) and Raman spectroscopy confirmed a rhombohedral structure, while scanning electron microscopy (SEM) and transmission electron microscopy (TEM) confirmed a nanoscale morphology. Notably, the 160$^{\circ}$C sample exhibited a significantly higher specific surface area compared to the bulk material. These nanopowders were evaluated for their photocatalytic performance in degrading Rhodamine B under UV light. The results demonstrated that the 160$^{\circ}$C NPs possessed superior photocatalytic activity relative to the bulk form, attributed to their enhanced surface area and the presence of surface defects.

We introduce a model featuring a $U(1)$ gauge symmetry alongside the Standard Model, which is extended by a $U(1)$-charged vector-like quark doublet. This setup generates a $Z'$ gauge boson and a new heavy Higgs singlet, which acquires a non-zero vacuum expectation value through electroweak symmetry breaking. The resulting single Higgs doublet with a vacuum expectation value ensures the absence of tree-level flavor-changing neutral currents. We calculate the $Z'$ mass and its branching ratios into various Standard Model particles, demonstrating that the proposed scenario remains consistent with current experimental data. Furthermore, we explore prospects for detecting the $Z'$ boson at the High-Luminosity Large Hadron Collider.

Reconstructing 3D hand-held objects from a single RGB image is a critical yet difficult task. Although recent methods have achieved promising results, they often fail to leverage the hand's intricate details and subtle movements. This study introduces a new approach that utilizes hand articulation to enhance the reconstruction of 3D hand-held objects from 2D images. We introduce a specialized module designed to extract the 3D object structure from a single RGB input. This module employs a multi-scale attention mechanism to isolate the hand's key features and then integrates this information with a pre-trained 2D object detector to generate 3D object representations. We also develop a new loss function that incorporates hand articulation to refine the 3D reconstruction process. Experiments on the H2O dataset demonstrate that our method outperforms existing state-of-the-art techniques, and our code is available at https://github.com/zhaojia1995/ArticulatedObject3D.

This study introduces a new method for deriving sunspot area from Kitt Peak photospheric magnetograms, which are subject to significant intensity inhomogeneities. By applying a new Equal Contrast technique, we demonstrate that these inhomogeneities are substantially reduced, leading to a correlation coefficient of 0.75 between Kitt Peak photospheric spot numbers and Ca-K line chromospheric spot numbers. This represents a substantial improvement over the previous best result of 0.58, which utilized the standard Maximum Intensity Difference method. Furthermore, the Equal Contrast approach yields a better agreement with the Ca-K line correlation than the traditional Minimum Intensity Difference method, which achieves a correlation coefficient of only 0.64.

This study reports the initial observation of the decay $\Sigma^+\to p\pi^0\gamma$ using $\propto$-proton-proton collisions at a center-of-mass energy of 13 TeV with a luminosity of 3.6 fb$^{-1}$ collected by the LHCb experiment. The analysis focuses on the $\Sigma^+\to p\pi^0\gamma$ decay chain, inferred from the final state comprising a proton and a neutral pion reconstructed via its decay into two photons. A localized excess of events is identified at a branching fraction of $1.6\times 10^{-8}$, situated 2.5 standard deviations from the standard model prediction, yielding a statistical significance of 2.5$\sigma$. No substantial variation is detected in the branching fraction across the invariant mass spectrum of the $p\pi^0$ system. The measured branching fraction is $(1.6\pm 0.2\text{(stat)}\pm 0.2\text{(syst)})\times 10^{-8}$.

Distributed symbolic execution (SE) has emerged as a viable approach to address the scalability challenges inherent in modern software systems. However, existing methods often fail to fully utilize the distributed computing environment, leading to redundant work and wasted resources. To address this, we introduce a new strategy for distributing SE that minimally increases implementation complexity while significantly enhancing execution efficiency. Our approach, called test-depth partitioning, organizes the program's control-flow graph into test statements and distributes them based on statement depth, ensuring that each distributed task contains a complete, independent test case. We evaluated this technique against two prevailing methods for distributed SE: one that assigns work at the statement level without depth consideration, and another that assigns work at the function level. Our results demonstrate that test-depth partitioning outperforms these baselines by 1.5x to 2.5x in terms of coverage, while cutting execution time by approximately 50%.

This study examines how the aspect ratio of magnetic nanoparticles influences their relaxation dynamics, specifically within a framework where dipolar interactions are weak. We analyze a system of non-interacting superparamagnets, where each particle is modeled as a collection of elementary magnetic moments. By employing a Monte Carlo approach, we calculate the relaxation times for various aspect ratios and dipolar interaction strengths. Our findings indicate that for low values of the dimensionless dipolar interaction parameter, the relaxation behavior remains consistent across different aspect ratios. Conversely, at high interaction strengths, the rate of relaxation becomes sensitive to the aspect ratio, exhibiting a non-monotonic dependence. Furthermore, we observe that the relaxation times are significantly impacted by the specific initial conditions of the system.

Federated Learning (FL) has emerged as a promising solution for privacy-sensitive scenarios, enabling the training of global models across decentralized devices without the exchange of raw data. However, the reliance on local model updates introduces significant risks, including data leakage and potential privacy breaches. To mitigate these risks, this paper introduces a new framework called Privacy-Preserving Federated Learning with Secure Aggregation (PPFL-SAG). PPFL-SAG integrates a novel secure aggregation protocol with a secure multi-party computation (MPC) approach to ensure the confidentiality of FL updates. By leveraging MPC, the system achieves robust protection against malicious participants, while the secure aggregation mechanism minimizes communication overhead. We provide a comprehensive analysis of PPFL-SAG's security properties and evaluate its performance using both synthetic and real-world datasets. Results indicate that PPFL-SAG effectively safeguards data privacy while maintaining competitive training efficiency compared to existing methods.

Short-text classification is a prevalent challenge in natural language processing, with Recurrent Neural Networks (RNNs) being a popular choice for handling sequential data. However, RNNs are often criticized for their slow inference times and high memory demands, which hinder their practical deployment. To address these limitations, we introduce a new approach that leverages the attention mechanism to capture dependencies between words within a text sequence. Our method utilizes a Transformer encoder to process the sequence and a classifier to determine the short text's category. Experimental results demonstrate that this model achieves superior performance compared to existing state-of-the-art short-text classifiers.

Chiplet technology offers a solution to the challenges of integrating multiple vendor-produced dies within a single chip, yet it also raises significant concerns regarding the potential for side-channel attacks to breach the confidentiality and integrity of these components. This study introduces a comprehensive framework designed to assess the security of chiplet-based architectures, with a specific focus on side-channel vulnerabilities. The work evaluates two primary attack vectors: interconnect-based attacks, which exploit the physical attributes of the communication links between dies, and memory-based attacks, which target the shared on-chip memory. Furthermore, the paper examines the specific side-channel threats faced by three distinct interconnect types—Ring, Crossbar, and Crossbar with Router (RC)—as well as the two memory configurations: Shared and Non-Shared. The analysis concludes that while the Shared memory configuration presents the highest risk, the RC memory variant is the most secure option. Additionally, the Non-Shared interconnect configuration is identified as the most robust against physical attacks.

Mixture cure models are designed to account for the limited potential of survival models by modeling the long-term fraction of patients who are effectively cured. This article introduces a Bayesian nonparametric approach to fitting mixture cure models, which offers greater flexibility than parametric models. The methodology relies on a new Dirichlet process mixture model that integrates a cure status indicator, allowing for a flexible estimation of the long-term cure rate. The model is estimated using a Gibbs sampling algorithm, and a new proposal for the Dirichlet process prior is introduced to enhance computational efficiency. The performance of the proposed model is evaluated through simulations and a real-world data analysis.

This paper investigates the nonlocal metric dimension of a graph, defined as the minimum number of vertices in a subset $S$ such that every vertex outside $S$ is distinguishable from each vertex in $S$ under a specific nonlocal separation criterion. We provide a concise algorithm capable of determining this nonlocal metric dimension for any given graph.

In recent years, in-memory computing (IMC) has garnered significant attention due to its potential to drastically reduce energy consumption and data transfer bottlenecks, making it a promising candidate for deep neural network (DNN) inference. However, IMC architectures are plagued by inherent nonlinearity and stochasticity stemming from analog devices, which severely degrade the accuracy of DNN models. To address this, we introduce a new DNN inference framework for IMC systems that integrates adaptive quantization with error correction. Specifically, we propose a quantization method that dynamically adjusts the number of bits allocated to each layer based on the inherent characteristics of the DNN model and the specific constraints of the IMC hardware. Furthermore, we develop an error correction mechanism designed to mitigate the impact of nonlinearities and noise, thereby enhancing inference precision. Experimental results demonstrate that our approach achieves substantial accuracy improvements across various DNN models when deployed on representative IMC platforms.

This paper introduces a new class of polar codes termed "large polarization kernels," which are constructed using specific large kernels and exhibit significantly enhanced polarization effects. These codes are designed to be shortened large polar kernels, offering advantages over polar codes built from kernels of smaller sizes. Specifically, the proposed shortened large polarization kernels enable the creation of polar codes featuring frozen bit positions that are more optimally arranged. Furthermore, a shortened variant of the $K_{16}$ kernel is presented, which not only maintains the advantages of large polarization kernels but also achieves a slightly higher weight gap compared to shortened versions of the $K_8$ and $K_{32}$ kernels.

Seismic data denoising is a critical challenge in the oil and gas industry, where deep learning methods have recently emerged as a promising solution. However, supervised deep learning approaches require large volumes of labeled training data, which are scarce in real-world scenarios. This study introduces a semi-supervised deep learning framework designed to denoise seismic datasets with limited ground truth annotations. The proposed method utilizes a U-Net architecture to process noisy data, incorporating a self-supervised auxiliary loss function that leverages the internal consistency of seismic signals. This strategy enables the model to effectively extract features from limited training examples and generalize to unseen noise patterns. Experimental results demonstrate that this approach achieves performance comparable to fully supervised models, while also confirming its efficacy in denoising datasets containing noise types not encountered during training.

The 2010 MOLLER experiment, designed to measure two-photon exchange effects in electron scattering, has been relocated to the new Hall D at Jefferson Lab. This new hall offers a significantly larger solid angle for detectors, enabling the study of these effects across a broader range of kinematics. This paper outlines the anticipated performance of the upgraded MOLLER spectrometers.

The Hubbard model serves as a foundational framework for investigating doped electrons or holes within an antiferromagnetic lattice, with strong on-site Coulomb repulsion being a primary focus. This work examines the half-filled Hubbard model on a honeycomb lattice, which hosts a chiral spin liquid phase, by analyzing the ground state phase diagram as a function of Coulomb interaction and hopping strength. We demonstrate that the system exhibits a phase diagram characterized by a competition between the chiral spin liquid and the Néel antiferromagnetic order. This analysis relies on a variational approach using a Gutzwiller projector applied to a reference state, which is a superposition of chiral spin liquid and Néel states. This method allows us to compute the ground state energy and the Gutzwiller parameter, which represents the probability of double occupancy. Our findings indicate that the chiral spin liquid phase is inherently stable and that the energy gap separating it from the Néel phase is substantial.

Mediation analysis is a prevalent method in social sciences for investigating the causal mechanisms linking predictors to outcomes. This paper presents a Bayesian framework for mediation analysis, which accommodates both categorical and continuous mediator types. This approach facilitates the estimation of average causal effects, including indirect effects mediated through the mediator, while accounting for the uncertainty inherent in these calculations. The methodology is evaluated using extensive simulations and is subsequently applied to a dataset from a randomized clinical trial.

A starshade is an external occulting device designed to block light from a target star, enabling the detection of faint nearby planets. This approach offers a viable alternative to coronagraphs and starshade telescopes, which rely on complex internal nulling mechanisms to achieve the necessary suppression of starlight. This paper outlines the design of a deployable, petal-shaped occulting screen capable of blocking starlight within a 100-milliradian (mrad) field of view, extending 100 mrad beyond the angular radius of a target planet's orbit. The proposed architecture utilizes a hexagonal framework of triangular units, where each petal consists of two curved trapezoidal sections. These sections are constructed from a single layer of thin, lightweight material, such as a polymer film, and are reinforced with a grid of structural ribs. The ribs are interconnected by flexible joints that allow the petal to bend, while the entire structure is supported by a central hub. This design ensures that the starshade can be deployed from a compact configuration to its full operational size in space. Detecting suicidal intent early is crucial for preventing fatalities, yet the scarcity of labeled data hinders the development of robust machine learning models. This paper introduces a new dataset comprising 1,000 suicide-related and 1,000 non-suicide-related posts from Reddit, featuring comprehensive annotations of semantic categories and linguistic markers. We present a novel ensemble model that leverages the strengths of both character-level and word embedding approaches to identify suicidal posts. Experimental results demonstrate that this method outperforms current state-of-the-art solutions. Finally, we discuss the challenges associated with this dataset and highlight the necessity for further research.

We present a framework for supersymmetric Schwarzians, which are defined as elements of superconformal groups that generate simple boundary residues. This framework extends the bosonic two-point function into a supersymmetric setting, yielding a proposed supersymmetric version of the Schwarzian derivative. We demonstrate that this generalization is not unique; rather, it admits a whole family of solutions characterized by an arbitrary number of real parameters. Furthermore, we establish the relationship between these Schwarzians and the corresponding one-point functions involving superprimary operators.

Qualitative characteristics of discrete dynamical systems are examined by analyzing difference equations of the form $x_{n+1}=f(x_n)$, where the function $f$ operates within a real interval. This study specifically addresses scenarios where $f$ is defined as a rational expression with positive coefficients. The analysis covers key solution behaviors, including monotonicity, boundedness, convergence, and periodicity, utilizing both analytical methods and numerical approaches.

This work examines the asymptotic behavior of Born-Infeld nonlinear electrodynamics within a curved spacetime framework. We derive the necessary equations for the nonlinear gauge field and establish the conditions under which a solution can be asymptotically flat.
