Although researchers have been investigating data collection and usage for over a decade, there is a notable lack of empirical studies addressing the feelings ordinary people hold regarding these practices. This paper addresses this gap by conducting a survey of 1,000 individuals to investigate their emotions toward current data collection and usage, and it offers a novel framework for categorizing these emotions alongside a corresponding measurement scale. The study findings reveal that the emotions identified are both prevalent and intense, and the survey outcomes provide a foundation for this proposed framework.

Faster-than-Nyquist (FTN) signaling enables higher spectral efficiency by deliberately inducing inter-symbol interference (ISI). However, this interference renders the received signal non-linear, necessitating a computationally intensive, iterative receiver that is impractical for real-time applications. To address this, we introduce a new linear receiver that approximates the optimal FTN solution by utilizing a linear approximation of the logarithm of the posterior probability. This proposed receiver significantly reduces computational complexity while maintaining performance levels comparable to the optimal receiver.

This work establishes that a complete atomic lattice effect algebra is equivalent to the structure formed by an order-continuous partial order on a complete set of atoms, thereby demonstrating that the complete lattice of effects within a von Neumann algebra adheres to the same organizational rules.

This paper introduces SaliencyMix, a data augmentation technique designed to enhance the performance of image classification models. The approach leverages class-specific saliency maps to determine the optimal combination of features from different source images. By integrating these high-impact features, SaliencyMix achieves superior results compared to standard Mixup and other existing Mixup variants. The proposed method is straightforward to implement and can be easily adapted to various existing data augmentation strategies. Experimental results on CIFAR-100 and ImageNet demonstrate that SaliencyMix consistently outperforms current Mixup variants. The accompanying code is publicly available at https://github.com/Cheng-Lin/SaliencyMix.

This study examines the bi-invariant convolution algebras of functions defined on subgroups of $GL_n(\mathbb{F}_q)$, where $\mathbb{F}_q$ is a finite field. We demonstrate that these algebras are isomorphic to the endomorphism rings of specific combinatorial structures, namely, collections of $k$-dimensional subspaces within $n$-dimensional vector spaces over $\mathbb{F}_q$. Furthermore, we establish that the endomorphism rings of these structures form a $p$-group (where $p$ is the characteristic of $\mathbb{F}_q$) precisely when $k$ is a multiple of $p$. Additionally, we identify the irreducible components of these algebras, thereby enabling a complete classification of their indecomposable modules.

Cosmic shear surveys are essential for mapping the large-scale structure of the universe, yet they are compromised by intrinsic alignments (IA) of galaxies, which are not caused by gravitational lensing. While previous studies have primarily focused on two-point correlations, this work examines the full spectrum of intrinsic shape correlations, ranging from n-point correlations to the complete joint probability distribution of shapes. We demonstrate that the IA contribution to n-point correlations can be precisely determined from the IA component of the first-point correlation, provided that n is greater than two. Furthermore, we find that the cumulative IA signal up to n-point correlations fully characterizes the joint probability distribution of intrinsic shapes. Consequently, future analyses of IA in cosmic shear surveys can be conducted with significantly reduced complexity.

Soft-deformable particle systems are widely utilized in both scientific research and industrial applications. Although these systems are known to exhibit shear stress softening under large deformations—characterized by a decline in shear stress and mechanical energy as strain increases—the underlying physical mechanisms remain poorly understood. This study investigates the nonlinear elastic and plastic properties of such systems through the lens of a modified version of the standard Drucker–Prager yield criterion. We demonstrate that the observed softening behavior arises from a strain-softening plastic response, driven by the system's evolving anisotropy. Furthermore, we establish a quantitative link between the yield criterion's parameters and the material's yield strength, Poisson's ratio, and shear modulus. By incorporating a yield criterion, we also clarify the intricate relationship between dissipated energy and shear strain. These findings offer a robust framework for analyzing the plasticity and failure mechanisms within soft-deformable matter.

Machine learning force fields (MLFFs) have recently become a powerful tool for investigating the atomic-scale dynamics of gold nanoparticles (AuNPs). However, the development of MLFFs for AuNPs has been hindered by the scarcity of experimental data, which is essential for refining interatomic potentials. This study introduces a novel MLFF designed for AuNPs, trained using a comprehensive dataset of 1,000 molecular dynamics trajectories. The training set encompasses diverse nanoparticle configurations, including various sizes, shapes, and surface terminations, as well as a wide range of temperatures. The resulting MLFF demonstrates exceptional accuracy in predicting the radial distribution function and heat capacity, and it effectively captures the temperature-dependent evolution of surface structures. Furthermore, the model exhibits strong transferability, accurately simulating systems with sizes outside the training range and temperatures beyond the initial training limits. The authors conclude that this MLFF is highly suitable for conducting extensive molecular dynamics simulations of AuNPs.
This paper establishes bifurcation theorems utilizing the univalent property of functionals. These results are demonstrated through the investigation of second-order nonlinear differential equations.

The Standard Model is characterized by its three fermion families, a feature that has led to a longstanding inquiry into whether these families are related. Grand Unified Theory (GUT) offers a potential explanation by housing all three families within a single gauge group. This paper investigates the possibility of a "GUT squared" scenario, wherein the three families arise from the tensor product of two distinct GUT representations. We demonstrate that such a construction is feasible only if the number of families is even, a constraint that contradicts the observed three families in nature. Furthermore, we explore the potential for extending this framework to accommodate four families.
This study establishes novel relations for $(h; q)$-Genocchi numbers and polynomials by applying the $(h; q)$-exponential generating function method to $h$-Bernstein polynomials of q-kind.

Randomized experiments are widely regarded as the gold standard for causal inference, yet their short duration often hinders the ability to measure long-term treatment impacts. To address this, researchers typically model long-term outcomes as functions of short-term outcomes, which are directly observed from the experiment. This paper introduces a new framework for estimating such relationships by leveraging data from both the experiment and a subsequent observational study. We develop a novel estimator that is both consistent and robust to violations of the experimental and observational studies' own assumption of random assignment. Furthermore, we establish the estimator's asymptotic normality and provide a closed-form approximation for its standard error. Finally, we demonstrate that our method outperforms existing approaches across various simulated scenarios and apply it to analyze the effects of a short-term intervention on long-term outcomes.

Case-control studies are frequently utilized to investigate rare diseases, yet they are susceptible to recall bias, which can compromise findings. This distortion occurs when participants with different exposure statuses remember past exposures differently. While the traditional approach involves adjusting for this bias through post-stratification, this study introduces a Bayesian framework that leverages external data to correct for it. This methodology is applicable to any study where external data regarding the exposure distribution exists. The proposed model is validated using a simulation study and a real-world case-control dataset concerning COVID-19 vaccination.

Autoencoders (AE) have proven effective for learning generative models of high-dimensional data distributions. However, their performance is often hindered by the difficulty of training deep generative architectures and the challenges associated with sampling from their learned distributions. To address these limitations, we introduce FLO (Autoencoders with Flows), a new framework that integrates Flows into autoencoders. This approach combines the benefits of both: the ability to map complex data distributions into a simple target space (like a Gaussian) using the flow's invertible transformations, while simultaneously leveraging the autoencoder's capacity to handle arbitrary input data. We demonstrate that FLOs achieve a significantly better balance between model expressiveness and sampling efficiency compared to standard VAEs. Additionally, we show that FLOs can be trained using a straightforward extension of the standard autoencoder loss function. Experiments on both synthetic and real-world datasets confirm that FLOs outperform both VAEs and GANs in terms of sampling efficiency and model expressiveness.

This paper introduces the concept of correlated attribute pattern (CAP) mining, a novel approach designed to uncover specific data patterns within urban sensing datasets. CAPs are defined as partial subgraphs in a data graph that share a common set of attributes. The study also outlines a new mining algorithm for identifying these structures, along with an evaluation of its computational complexity. Additionally, the authors demonstrate the practical utility of CAP mining by applying it to the analysis of urban sensing data.

This study introduces a novel, robust, and fully discrete Hybridizable Discontinuous Galerkin (HDG) approach for addressing the reaction-diffusion system and the generalized Stokes equations. The proposed method features a unique formulation that integrates a generalized pressure variable with the standard method's variables, thereby eliminating the need for approximating pressure directly. This strategy yields a significantly reduced linear system, as the only unknowns approximated on element boundaries are the flux normal components. Theoretical analysis confirms that the method is stable and achieves an optimal convergence rate. Furthermore, numerical experiments demonstrate the approach's robustness and validate its effectiveness.

Missing outcome data remains a prevalent challenge in clinical trials, and Sensitivity Analysis serves as a standard method for evaluating how robust findings are to unmeasured factors driving missingness. This paper introduces a novel Sensitivity Analysis framework for clinical trials featuring binary time-to-event outcomes affected by missing data. The proposed approach utilizes a latent variable model to address missingness, with parameters estimated via a weighted likelihood method. This methodology offers several advantages: it can be implemented using existing software, accommodates multiple imputation strategies, and allows for the assessment of various plausible assumptions regarding the data. Furthermore, the study demonstrates that this new method yields equivalent results to alternative missingness models under specific conditions. The efficacy of the proposed technique is validated through both a simulation study and a practical application.

In the context of analyzing gene expression data from crossover trials, which frequently suffer from missing values, we evaluate two methods for handling these gaps: the conventional maximum likelihood estimator (MLE) and the Bayesian estimator (BE). Our analysis demonstrates that the Bayesian approach consistently outperforms the traditional MLE. To substantiate this claim, we present a novel derivation of the complete likelihood function for linear mixed models under the assumption of missing responses. Furthermore, we introduce a streamlined algorithm for computing the BE, which proves to be more efficient than the standard MLE procedure.

We define the $A_n$ structure as a lax symmetric monoidal algebra within a category of $A$-modules, where $A$ is a symmetric monoid. We then establish a connection between $A_n$ structures and $n$-fold loop spaces. Specifically, we demonstrate that an $A_n$ structure on an object $X$ is equivalent to an $n$-fold loop space structure on that same object. This result extends to the context of $\infty$-categories.

DRAM is a widely utilized memory technology, yet its fixed internal timing constraints hinder its ability to meet diverse application needs. To address this, we introduce P-DRAM, a novel DRAM architecture that enables programmable internal timings. By allowing the control of internal DRAM timings, P-DRAM achieves two key objectives: (1) it mitigates data loss caused by bit-coupling, thereby enhancing reliability, and (2) it facilitates DRAM-assisted computing, which improves overall energy efficiency and performance. To support these capabilities, we developed a P-DRAM hardware design featuring a programmable timing controller and a corresponding memory interface. Furthermore, we devised a P-DRAM memory scheduler to optimize the scheduling of memory requests. Our results demonstrate that P-DRAM can reduce data loss by up to 99.9% and achieve a 1.55× speedup. Additionally, P-DRAM-assisted computing delivers substantial gains, including up to 1.8× higher performance and 2.7× better energy efficiency, compared to traditional DRAM.

Network Functions Virtualization (NFV) represents a key strategy for the future evolution of telecommunications networks, enabling the efficient, cost-effective, and flexible deployment of network operations by virtualizing functions on commercial off-the-shelf hardware. This shift necessitates a new approach to resource management, where network functions are instantiated on virtual machines within data centers. This paper introduces a novel, multi-layered NFV orchestration framework designed to optimize the allocation of virtual network function (VNF) resources across a heterogeneous pool of servers. The proposed solution utilizes a two-layer architecture: a first layer dedicated to VNF placement and a second layer handling VNF scaling. To address the complex challenges of these tasks, we employ a multi-objective optimization approach that balances multiple criteria. The system is designed to be flexible, allowing users to define specific optimization goals. The paper further details the mathematical models, the algorithmic design, and the implementation of this framework.

Quantum error correction (QEC) is essential for achieving fault-tolerant quantum computation, yet the high overhead associated with current QEC codes often hinders their practical application. This work introduces a method to reduce the resource costs required for QEC codes by leveraging quantum circuits that utilize multi-qubit gates. We demonstrate that the use of these gates can significantly lower the number of physical qubits needed to implement a logical qubit. Specifically, we apply this approach to the surface code, deriving a new variant that utilizes $d^2$ physical qubits per logical qubit, where $d$ represents the distance parameter. Furthermore, we introduce a generalized framework for constructing surface codes with $k$ logical qubits using $n_d$ physical qubits per logical qubit, where $n_d$ is an odd integer. This framework accommodates various configurations, including those with fewer physical qubits than the standard $2d+1$ per logical qubit. We also examine the impact of multi-qubit gates on the code's distance and the complexity of implementing stabilizer measurements. Ultimately, our findings suggest that employing multi-qubit gates can substantially enhance the efficiency of QEC implementations.

OPUS represents a flexible framework designed to facilitate the integration of analysis and simulation tools with experimental data. Built upon the ROOT project's data model and abstraction, OPUS enables data-centric handling of information from diverse origins, including files and remote databases. It offers a streamlined method for combining datasets from different sources, performing calculations, and executing complex queries. The system's modular architecture allows for the creation of specialized tools tailored to specific experimental setups. Additionally, OPUS supports the visualization of results through integration with existing software libraries.

Digital Game-Based Learning (DGBL) has become a vital component of modern education, offering an engaging and effective method to enhance student experience. This paper introduces a DGBL prototype designed to support undergraduate engineering education. The system's architecture is built on a layered model, utilizing the Unity engine for the game interface and a custom backend for managing the educational content.

Molecular oxygen (O2) and ozone (O3) are essential for life on Earth, with O2 originating from photosynthesis and O3 forming photochemically from O2. While Earth's O2 levels are regulated by biological processes, O3 is produced photochemically from O2 and is sensitive to solar UV radiation. Consequently, O3 serves as a proxy for UV intensity in the atmosphere. This study examines the relationship between O2 and O3 in the atmospheres of exoplanets, specifically those with Earth-like conditions. We developed a model to determine the equilibrium concentration of O3 given fixed O2 levels and UV radiation intensity. Our results indicate that the O3/O2 ratio is highly sensitive to UV radiation levels, potentially reaching up to 100 times higher than Earth's ratio under low UV conditions. This sensitivity could be utilized to infer the stellar UV radiation received by exoplanets, offering a method to detect habitable zones around stars with different spectral characteristics.

This study introduces a three-dimensional lattice framework for robust crosscurrents, designed to maintain stability against defects and disorder. By extending the principles of two-dimensional robust current systems, we develop a three-dimensional model that generates robust current flows along three orthogonal axes. Unlike previous two-dimensional models, the currents in our proposed system are not constrained by specific boundary conditions. Furthermore, we identify a broad parameter range where the robustness of these currents remains intact despite the presence of impurities. Theoretically, we demonstrate that the resilience of two-dimensional robust systems naturally extends to three dimensions, ensuring stability against impurities. Additionally, we provide a numerical analysis of how impurities influence the robust current in three dimensions, confirming that the system's resilience remains effective within a wide span of parameters.

Multilingual neural machine translation (MNMT) models have demonstrated the ability to enhance translation quality for low-resource languages by leveraging abundant parallel data from closely related languages. This study introduces a new approach to expanding MNMT by integrating monolingual corpora, a method designed to increase model capacity and mitigate the data scarcity issue prevalent in low-resource languages. We evaluate this technique on the OPUScrosslingual dataset, focusing on the translation of the less-resourced Burmese language. Our findings indicate that incorporating monolingual data substantially improves model performance, with a specific language model fine-tuned on monolingual corpora yielding the best outcomes.

This study examines the formation of dust-acoustic ion-ion cyclotron waves in a dusty plasma environment consisting of positively charged dust and ions, alongside electrons following a non-isotropic Maxwellian distribution. By employing a reductive perturbation technique, the authors derived a modified Korteweg-de Vries-Cercignani (MKdC) equation. The analysis highlights that these specific waves are driven by the presence of charged dust. Furthermore, the research investigates how the presence of an external magnetic field influences the specific characteristics of these waves.

Recent developments in dense retrieval have demonstrated the effectiveness of pretrained language models (PLMs) in generating high-quality embeddings. However, the computational costs associated with these models often hinder their application in large-scale retrieval scenarios. To address this, we introduce a new approach that leverages the semantic alignment between PLMs and semantic word vectors. By utilizing a multilingual vectorization model, we convert query and document text into compact PLM-based word vectors. This method enables the training of an efficient, lightweight bilinear model capable of matching multilingual queries and documents. Our multilingual vectorization model achieves state-of-the-art performance on multilingual dense retrieval tasks, while the resulting lightweight model attains competitive results on dense retrieval benchmarks in both English and Spanish.

Multimodal learning (MML) aims to enhance performance by leveraging complementary information from diverse data sources, such as text and images. While existing MML methods typically rely on a single fusion strategy, they often fail to adapt to varying data characteristics, leading to suboptimal results. To address this, we introduce a novel MML framework that employs multiple fusion strategies, each designed to capture distinct multimodal relationships. Furthermore, we implement a gating mechanism to dynamically select the optimal strategy for each sample based on its specific characteristics. To ensure the chosen strategy aligns with the sample's underlying data properties, we incorporate a gate predictor that learns to identify these features. We investigate massless fermions within a relativistic quantum framework, specifically focusing on the non-perturbative regime where vector and axial vector currents are present. Our analysis demonstrates that the Wilsonian effective action for these massless fermions can be fully characterized by a single real function, $F$, which is determined by the divergence of the axial vector current. Furthermore, we establish that the Wilsonian effective action for massless fermions coupled to a background $SU(2)$ Yang-Mills field is uniquely defined by two real functions, $F_1$ and $F_2$, derived from the divergence of the axial vector current and the chiral anomaly, respectively. These findings are consistent with the chiral magnetic and chiral vortical effects.

This study introduces a novel, end-to-end spoken command recognition system built on a tensor-train network designed to handle diverse utterances of identical commands. The proposed architecture utilizes a tensor-train graph composed of multiple tensor-train layers, where each layer represents a specific word in the command sequence. To address variations in how commands are spoken, the framework incorporates a hidden state mechanism within each graph layer, enabling the modeling of utterance-level dynamics. To train this model, the research employs a newly developed tensor-decomposition-based likelihood function. The method is evaluated on the Google Speech Commands dataset, where it achieves state-of-the-art performance.

Quantum-jump unravelings are a standard and broadly utilized framework for describing open quantum systems. Although they are widely adopted, their specific physical meaning has remained somewhat ambiguous. This paper clarifies that such unravelings correspond to a discrete-time stochastic process that converges to a stochastic differential equation in the continuous-time limit. By formulating this underlying discrete model, we reveal a direct connection between quantum-jump dynamics and the quantum trajectory concept introduced by Carmichael. Furthermore, we demonstrate that this approach is adaptable to various formulations of unravelings and extends to scenarios involving classical randomness in the Hamiltonian.

The optical absorption within silicon nanoparticle solar cells is heavily influenced by the nanoparticles' geometries. This research investigates how the absorption characteristics of these devices change when transitioning from spherical nanoparticles to ellipsoidal ones, specifically by varying the ellipsoidal aspect ratio. Our findings indicate that, for a given volume, the ellipsoidal configuration can achieve a broader absorption spectrum compared to the spherical counterpart. Furthermore, we demonstrate that a specific optimal aspect ratio maximizes the short-circuit current density in the solar cell.

We introduce a novel logical framework designed to precisely characterize problems solvable in deterministic polynomial time. This system extends first-order logic with a least fixed point operator, utilizing a specific set of permitted fixed point definitions. By capitalizing on a recent breakthrough by A. A. Bulatov and I. A. Dobrits regarding the classification of first-order logic with fixed points, we demonstrate that the complexity of evaluating formulas within our language falls into dichotomous categories: either the task is tractable in polynomial time, or it is $\textsc{\#P}$-hard.

LSTMs are widely employed for sequence prediction, yet they often demand substantial data and computational resources. This study introduces a novel, low-complexity LSTM framework that leverages a multi-resolution approach to enhance efficiency. The methodology involves segmenting input sequences into distinct parts, each with varying resolutions, and processing them through parallel LSTM modules. The outputs of these parallel components are subsequently merged via a multi-resolution fusion mechanism. This architecture is designed to retain the precision of standard LSTMs while significantly lowering computational complexity. The proposed model is evaluated across two domains: time series forecasting and natural language processing. Results indicate that the new architecture outperforms existing state-of-the-art low-complexity methods, delivering accuracy comparable to full-sized LSTMs.

MAVLink is a lightweight communication protocol designed for the Internet of Drones (IoD), serving as the standard for data exchange between unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) and their ground control stations (GCS). Despite its widespread adoption, MAVLink is susceptible to several security vulnerabilities, including packet injection, replay attacks, and denial-of-service (DoS) attacks. This paper introduces a new framework for securing the MAVLink protocol, specifically targeting the protocols used in the main flight control loop. The proposed architecture is built upon the concept of a trusted module, which is integrated into the flight controller to ensure the confidentiality and integrity of critical data. This module is engineered to be adaptable across various flight controllers, thereby enhancing the security of the MAVLink protocol. The framework's effectiveness is validated through a case study involving a quadcopter equipped with an ArduCopter flight controller.

The performance of extensive distributed systems is heavily influenced by network characteristics such as latency, bandwidth, and reliability. This paper introduces a novel framework for automatically generating distributed applications designed to optimize these specific network attributes. The approach utilizes a declarative language to describe application behavior, paired with an automatic synthesis tool that constructs distributed programs capable of meeting user-specified performance targets. By modeling the system as a Markov Decision Process (MDP), the method employs Markov Decision Process (MDP)-based synthesis to produce network-efficient distributed applications. We have developed a prototype of this framework and evaluated it against various network scenarios. The experimental results demonstrate that the generated applications significantly outperform manually written ones in terms of network efficiency.

This study examines a specific subset of self-dual solutions to vacuum Maxwell equations defined over four-dimensional Euclidean space, utilizing the Penrose-Ward correspondence to translate these solutions into solutions of four-dimensional Einstein's equations featuring self-dual Ricci curvature. The analysis demonstrates that this generated class of gravitational solutions encompasses both the Taub-NUT and Kerr-Taub-NUT metrics. The paper concludes by exploring the characteristics of this solution set and providing a derivation of these new solutions via twistor theory.

This paper introduces a novel muon-based technique designed to analyze the subterranean architecture of the Great Pyramid of Giza. The proposed method involves deploying a detector array at the pyramid's base to capture cosmic muons that have traversed the structure. By analyzing the spatial distribution of detected muons, researchers can reconstruct internal density distributions and potentially identify concealed chambers. The study outlines a novel algorithm for this reconstruction and demonstrates its efficacy through simulations of a model pyramid containing hidden rooms.

Parsing expression grammars (PEGs) are a widely adopted formalism for defining structured text formats, having been adopted by numerous parsing libraries. Central to PEGs is ordered choice, which dictates that the left-hand option of a choice is selected unless it fails to match, thereby establishing a precedence hierarchy among alternatives. This work introduces a new concept, ordered nonbacktracking choice, which merges the hierarchical structure of ordered choice with the exhaustive evaluation of a traditional deterministic parser. We demonstrate that PEGs featuring this updated construct can be compiled into a single deterministic pushdown automaton. Consequently, this approach offers an efficient solution for parsing unstructured data, such as HTML, JSON, and XML.

This paper investigates the temperature-dependent Cherenkov radiation of a scalar particle by a fermion within a hot scalar QED framework, utilizing the real-time formalism of finite temperature field theory. We derive the fermion's one-loop self-energy and calculate the corresponding Cherenkov rate, which represents the probability of a hot scalar emitting off a relativistic fermion. Our findings indicate a linear increase in the rate as temperature rises, a behavior attributed to the thermal population of scalar particles. At extremely high temperatures, the rate exhibits a power-law suppression due to the fermion acquiring thermal mass. Furthermore, we examine how the rate is influenced by the coupling constant and various scalar and fermion masses.

Recent research indicates that electroencephalography (EEG) signals during language processing reflect the brain's ongoing modeling of input through neural representations of language. This study introduces a new method for quantifying predictability by utilizing state-of-the-art language models, which are then benchmarked against traditional linguistic frameworks. We evaluated three distinct categories of models: a cutting-edge transformer-based system (BERT), a standard n-gram approach, and a classic bigram method. Our findings demonstrate that BERT achieves superior predictability scores compared to the other models. Notably, these scores effectively capture a substantial portion of the EEG data explained by both word co-occurrence and linguistic variables. These results suggest that neural language models may serve as a robust proxy for the cognitive processes engaged when humans comprehend language.

Accurately estimating the 3D pose of objects from a single image is a critical and difficult challenge in computer vision. Although recent methods have achieved promising results, they largely depend on synthetic data generated from 3D models, which often fail to capture the visual diversity and complexity of real-world environments. This paper introduces a new approach to single-view 3D object pose estimation that leverages in-the-wild video data. By utilizing the temporal consistency inherent in videos, we can derive more robust 3D object poses. Our methodology involves a two-stage process: first, we employ a video-based 3D pose estimation network to generate initial poses, followed by a refinement step that leverages these outputs to correct errors. This refinement utilizes a new 3D pose loss function designed to explicitly penalize deviations from the model's surface. Experimental results on the 3D-Pose and 2.5D-POS-E datasets demonstrate that our approach outperforms existing state-of-the-art methods.

We investigate the coupling between Majorana bound states and phonons in semiconductor-superconductor heterostructures, where Andreev bound states (ABS) serve as a primary mechanism for interaction. This coupling is mediated by phonons through their modulation of the superconducting order parameter's amplitude. We demonstrate that the resulting phonon-mediated ABS relaxation rates are heavily influenced by the ABS energy spectrum, particularly in regimes where subgap minibands exist. Our analysis indicates that the resulting ABS relaxation rates can be orders of magnitude lower than those driven by electron interactions, potentially enabling the observation of exceptionally long Majorana zero modes lifetimes.

Particle acceleration via magnetic reconnection is a prevalent mechanism across various astrophysical plasmas, including solar flares, pulsar magnetospheres, and accretion disks. This study introduces a new framework for modeling particle acceleration driven by reconnection within a 3D relativistic context. The approach employs a hybrid of kinetic and fluid simulations, utilizing a fluid-based, fully relativistic, 3D magnetohydrodynamics code to model the reconnection dynamics, while integrating particle-in-cell methods to handle re-acceleration. We validate this methodology by benchmarking it against a fully kinetic, 3D relativistic hybrid simulation. The results demonstrate that the new hybrid approach effectively reproduces the key characteristics of particle acceleration in relativistic reconnection scenarios.

This study examines the impact of one-loop corrections on the Higgsstrahlung ($e^+e^- \to ZH$) process within an extended scalar sector. We compute the impact of these corrections on the cross-section for the full chain $e^+e^- \to ZH \to e^+e^-Z$ and the partial chain $e^+e^- \to ZH \to Z\gamma$, utilizing an extended scalar sector that introduces new contributions to the Higgsstrahlung vertex. Our findings indicate that these corrections can substantially influence the process.

This paper examines the subdifferential of the joint numerical radius within multi-operator spaces. It establishes that the subdifferential corresponds to the normal structure found in joint numerical radius-level sets. Additionally, we introduce a concept of a "junta unit" that is closely connected to the joint numerical radius. The study also provides an alternative definition of the joint numerical radius using the concept of a "junta unit." Finally, we explore the connections between the joint numerical radius and the operator norm.

Deep learning has become a cornerstone of modern artificial intelligence, with its applications extending into financial trading. This study examines the privacy and security ramifications of deploying such frameworks within finance. We demonstrate that financial market data can be successfully reconstructed from the trained parameters of neural networks, even when these models are trained on proprietary datasets. Furthermore, we show that an adversary can effectively leverage a single trading model to illicitly profit from insider trading. To address these vulnerabilities, we propose a novel defensive strategy that conceals the specific identity of assets within the network architecture, thereby mitigating the potential for data reconstruction and insider trading exploitation.

This study investigates the Hilbert space framework for multivariate second-order stochastic processes. We demonstrate that these mappings possess reproducing kernel properties and establish a connection to the concept of operator-valued kernels. Furthermore, we examine the multivariate covariance operator, elucidating its relationship with the reproducing kernel structure. The work also introduces a spectral representation tailored to these multivariate second-order stochastic processes.

This study introduces a new ignition model for high-pressure hydrogen-oxygen mixtures, which diverges from the conventional assumption that the process is entirely stochastic. The model posits that ignition is non-random, driven instead by the activation of seed electrons that initiate electron avalanches. The probability of ignition is defined as the likelihood that these avalanches reach a critical threshold capable of triggering a thermal runaway. The research demonstrates that the model accurately predicts the maximum energy required to initiate ignition across a range of pressures, temperatures, and mixture compositions. Furthermore, it establishes that the maximum energy does not follow a monotonic trend with respect to mixture density, and it identifies an optimal density for each temperature that minimizes the energy needed for ignition.

Accurate image segmentation is essential for various applications, including medical diagnosis and autonomous driving. This paper introduces a Boundary-Aware Segmentation Network (BSAN) designed to enhance segmentation precision by integrating specialized modules for boundary awareness and context. The BSN framework comprises a backbone network, a boundary-aware module, and a context-aware module. The backbone network employs a multi-scale feature fusion strategy to generate multi-scale features, while the boundary-aware module utilizes a multi-scale boundary attention mechanism to identify critical boundary regions. Furthermore, the context-aware module incorporates a multi-scale context attention mechanism to capture global semantic information. The proposed BSN architecture is evaluated on the Cityscapes dataset for street scene segmentation. The results demonstrate that BSN outperforms existing state-of-the-art methods, achieving an mIoU of 74.8% on the Cityscapes validation set. The project source code is publicly available at https://github.com/kuangliang/Boundary-Aware-Segmentation-Network.

Vehicle-to-Everything (V2X) communication empowers Connected and Autonomous Vehicles (CAVs) to acquire situational awareness of their surroundings, thereby enhancing safety and traffic flow efficiency. This paper introduces a novel framework for managing CAVs that integrates communication capabilities with deep reinforcement learning (DRL). The approach utilizes a multi-agent architecture where each vehicle independently learns to navigate through intersections. The system is evaluated using a simulator built on SUMO and Pyv2x, featuring a custom training environment for CAVs. Results indicate that this proposed method surpasses existing state-of-the-art techniques in both traffic efficiency and safety.

We investigate analytically and numerically the behavior of active particles confined within a two-dimensional channel. The system consists of two particle types: strongly active particles that rotate randomly and are driven by thermal noise, and weakly active particles that rotate slowly and are governed by a self-propulsion force. Our analysis reveals that increasing the activity of weak particles leads to a corresponding rise in their density and flow rates near the boundaries. Furthermore, we demonstrate that this phenomenon arises from a phase transition characterized by a discontinuous change in weak particle density.

Electronic states within plasmas are traditionally modeled using either a discrete spectrum for bound levels or a continuous spectrum for free states. Siegert states, recently identified in quantum mechanics as an alternative representation for both bound and free states, are explored here in the context of plasma physics. These states are defined as solutions to the Schrödinger equation featuring complex energy eigenvalues and oscillatory behavior with decaying amplitude extending to infinity. The authors demonstrate that a specific set of Siegert states can fully describe a plasma's electronic states, wherein the imaginary components of their energy eigenvalues correspond to the ionization rates of Rydberg levels. Furthermore, it is shown that the orthogonality relations inherent to Siegert states facilitate the derivation of an equation of motion for the time-dependent wave function, yielding results equivalent to those obtained via the complex absorbing potential method.

We examine the impact of the topological $\theta$-term within the lattice formulation of quantum chromodynamics (QCD). This term introduces a topological susceptibility that scales with the inverse of the lattice spacing, $a^4$, thereby inducing a significant increase in the Coulombic component of the color field confinement mechanism. Consequently, this leads to a pronounced enhancement of the string tension, a phenomenon that contradicts physical reality. We demonstrate that this inconsistency arises because the $\theta$-term fails to generate a confining potential when analyzed via the Abelian projection method.

This study examines how the critical angle for ion-beam irradiation varies with incident angle, ion species, energy, and film thickness. The investigation utilizes the TRIDYN simulation code to model the evolution of the amorphization depth profile. Results indicate that this critical angle is dependent on ion species, energy, and thickness, but remains unaffected by the thickness of the amorphous layer. Furthermore, the proposed methodology for determining the critical angle is validated against experimental data from studies involving Ga$^+$ and Si$^{4+}$ ions.

Source code anti-plagiarism systems utilize cryptography to safeguard code integrity and ensure authenticity. Two primary methods are employed: a hash function to guarantee integrity and a digital signature to provide non-repudiation. This paper introduces a new approach that leverages both cryptographic properties to verify code integrity. The proposed algorithm operates in two stages: first, it employs a digital signature to authenticate its self, followed immediately by a hash function to confirm the integrity of associated source code.

We establish the growth of coefficients for a specific Dirichlet series, denoted as $f(s)$, which possesses a pole of order $d$ at $s=1$ and converges for all arguments where $\sigma > d$. The result demonstrates that $|\xi_n| = O(n^{\frac{d-1}{2} \ln n} + n^{d-1})$.

We establish that for any pair of natural numbers $k$ and $r$, every finitely generated subgroup $\Gamma$ of $\mathrm{GL}_n(\mathbb{Z})$ possesses a $(k,r)$-metric approximate subgroup consisting entirely of elements from $\Gamma$. Consequently, this result demonstrates that such groups are dense under metrics with exponents $k$ relative to any open set containing $\Gamma$ that is invariant under conjugation.

Estimating log-concave densities is a cornerstone of nonparametric inference, with the log-concave density class enjoying broad practical utility. This paper introduces a new estimator for log-concave densities that incorporates external covariates, specifically addressing scenarios where data consist of log-concave samples paired with associated predictors. The proposed estimator is derived by maximizing a log-likelihood function that is inherently non-concave but exhibits a piecewise linear concave structure. We prove that this estimator is both strongly consistent in distribution and asymptotically efficient. Furthermore, we demonstrate that the resulting estimator for the log-concave function is piecewise linear and that the estimated density's kurtosis and variance are both bounded. Simulation studies reveal that the new estimator performs comparably to the standard estimator lacking covariates. Finally, the method is applied to analyze data from the National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey (NHANES) to estimate the distribution of human body mass index (BMI).

This study introduces a Wang-Landau algorithm designed to sample static configurations in granular systems, utilizing a configuration space defined by a set of contact numbers. The approach employs a simulated-annealing strategy to achieve a uniform density of states estimate across this space. By applying the method to a system of $N=20$ frictionless spheres within a two-dimensional square box, we demonstrate the successful generation of a uniform distribution of contacts. Furthermore, the method's versatility is highlighted by its applicability to various granular system variants, including those involving friction, polydisperse particles, and complex geometries.

The Explorer-Director game is a two-player puzzle played on a graph $G$ with $n$ vertices and $m$ edges. In each round, the Explorer reveals a vertex $v$; if the count of edges incident to $v$ is less than $m/n$, the Director wins immediately. Following this, the Director must declare a new target vertex for the Explorer to uncover. The Explorer's objective is to avoid losing as long as possible, while the Director seeks to minimize the total number of rounds required to force a win. The game's "passage time" is defined as the maximum number of rounds needed for the Director to secure a win starting from any initial configuration. This paper establishes a straightforward upper bound on passage time, demonstrating that it does not exceed $O(\sqrt{nm} \log n)$.

This study examines the time-dependent scaling of the variance and frequency-frequency correlation in the frequency domain for two stochastic processes: Brownian motion and the Ornstein-Uhlenbeck process. We demonstrate that these properties are governed by the process's time-domain power spectrum and its corresponding time-frequency coherence function. By applying a time-frequency Wigner-Ville distribution to the process, we derive the second moment of this function to quantify the frequency-frequency correlation.

This paper investigates interaction solutions for the higher-order Broer-Kaup system, comprising distinct solitary, periodic, and kink profiles. Interaction scenarios occurring between pairs of these exact nonlinear excitations—specifically soliton-soliton, soliton-periodic, kink-periodic, and soliton-kink combinations—are derived analytically. These interaction solutions are presented graphically, with their physical significance clarified through the analysis of limiting conditions.

This study examines the incompressible Euler equations under the influence of an external magnetic field. We demonstrate that the energy of the fluid solution remains bounded, even if the vorticity is not bounded. This finding is derived by deriving a new criterion linking the evolution of energy to the vorticity's behavior.

VIRUP is a virtual reality system designed to enable users to navigate and explore extensive datasets. By leveraging contemporary VR hardware, VIRUP delivers a highly immersive and fluid experience. This paper introduces VIRUP, detailing its architecture, implementation, and the development process of its accompanying application. We also outline the specific steps taken to create our VIRUP application and evaluate the project's outcomes.

This paper presents a pedagogical approach to data education that leverages the versatility of LEGO bricks to construct tangible data structures. By enabling students to physically build datasets, the method allows for the immediate collection of data through simple experiments and the subsequent visualization of these findings using physical graphs. The study evaluates this framework within a live classroom environment involving students aged 10 to 12, demonstrating that the approach effectively supports the acquisition of core concepts in data analysis.

This study addresses the challenge of identifying functional data paths in a Software Defined Networking (SDN) environment, where a central controller manages the network by issuing instructions to switches. The problem is defined as determining if a specific path exists between a source and a destination, given a set of switches and their current operational status. We introduce a novel algorithm that determines the necessary and sufficient conditions for uncovering such functional routes. Furthermore, we demonstrate that this problem is NP-hard, presenting a formal proof for this complexity. To address the specific scenario where a single blocked switch obstructs an otherwise functional path, we provide a polynomial-time algorithm. Additionally, we present another algorithm designed to efficiently locate a valid operational path in a scenario involving multiple blocked switches.

Although disentangling neural representations is a significant objective, enforcing disentanglement within the training process remains a difficult challenge. This paper introduces a new method for enforcing such constraints in the feature space, utilizing a specialized disentanglement layer that can be integrated into existing architectures. This approach is compatible with both supervised and unsupervised learning, as well as self-supervised techniques. The layer's design is based on a specific metric that quantifies disentanglement, which is optimized during the training phase. Additionally, the method's efficiency is enhanced by employing a computationally efficient approximation of the underlying calculation.

This study examines energy harvesting from hydrokinetic flows using two NACA0012 foils arranged in tandem. The analysis focuses on the impact of varying gap distances on the performance of both individual foils and the system as a whole. The results indicate that, within the range of 0.5 to 3.0 non-dimensional gaps, the system achieves its maximum power coefficient of 0.42 at a gap of 1.0. This peak efficiency occurs at a reduced frequency of 1.4, where the downstream foil is significantly more active than its upstream counterpart. This disparity arises because the downstream foil is positioned within the wake of the upstream foil, facilitating a resonance between the flow and the downstream foil's natural frequency.

This paper examines the application of Bayesian inference for extracting spectral functions from lattice QCD simulations, a process that is computationally demanding and prone to numerical instabilities. We introduce a novel prior spectral function, constructed as a Gaussian mixture model, which is specifically designed to minimize the computational load associated with Monte Carlo Markov Chain sampling. Additionally, we present a method for deriving spectral functions from correlation functions computed on the lattice, utilizing an efficient algorithm to calculate the full Bayesian posterior probability density function. This approach facilitates the extraction of key spectral characteristics, including mass spectra and decay widths, directly from non-perturbative correlation data.

We introduce a technique for detecting charge tunneling between a quantum dot and a superconducting island, utilizing the quantum dot as a single-electron transistor. This method relies on the proximity-induced Andreev reflection phenomenon. We demonstrate that this approach enables the measurement of Andreev level energy within a superconducting island, thereby facilitating the study of quantum phase slips and other superconducting phenomena. Furthermore, we illustrate how this method can be used to investigate the parity switching between the superconducting island and the quantum dot.

Drug targets are fundamental to disease pathogenesis, and identifying novel ones is essential for developing new therapeutics. While recent advancements in knowledge graph embedding (KGE) have enabled the discovery of drug-disease associations, few studies have utilized KGE to uncover drug targets. This research introduces a framework that integrates drug-target and disease-target association networks to derive novel drug targets. The system employs a two-stage process: first, it utilizes a specific KGE model to embed the disease-target network; second, it applies a standard KGE model to embed the drug-target network, using the disease-specific embeddings. The final output is a ranked list of candidate drug targets for each specific disease. Evaluated on a public dataset, the framework successfully retrieved known disease targets with high precision. Furthermore, it identified several novel targets for established diseases that were subsequently validated through literature review.

This study examines implementation strategies for lambda-calculus by focusing on the interplay between call-by-value and call-by-name evaluation within a framework that integrates both. The analysis explores the theoretical underpinnings, establishes a formal semantics for hybrid strategies, and details the specific behaviors of the proposed system. Furthermore, the study assesses these strategies against criteria of expressiveness and efficiency, utilizing both theoretical and experimental evidence.

The Small Magellanic Cloud (SMC) and Large Magellanic Cloud (LMC) represent a binary system of interacting galaxies, with the LMC acting as the dominant partner. This interaction has significantly influenced the chemical evolution of the SMC, notably through the accretion of LMC material. This study investigates the chemical properties of the SMC by analyzing the abundances of 12 elements (O, Na, Al, Mg, Si, Ca, Ti, Fe, S, Ar, Ni, and Ge) in 140 SMC stars, utilizing high-resolution spectra from the VLT/UVES and VLT/X-Shooter instruments. The results indicate that the SMC exhibits a metal-poor profile with a mean metallicity of [Fe/H] = -2.10 ± 0.05, a value consistent with prior research. Furthermore, we observe a strong correlation between [Fe/H] and [α/Fe] ratios, suggesting that the SMC's chemical enrichment was primarily driven by a single burst of star formation. Additionally, we detect a significant anti-correlation between [Na/Fe] and [Fe/H], implying that the SMC has experienced chemical enrichment from LMC material. Finally, we calculate the total mass of heavy elements accreted from the LMC to be approximately 1.3 × 10⁷ solar masses.

Smart grids are susceptible to electricity theft, which can be detected by analyzing consumption patterns. This study introduces a novel method for identifying theft by applying deep recurrent neural networks to consumption data. The proposed model utilizes a Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) network to forecast energy usage and employs the discrepancies between these predictions and actual values to flag theft incidents. To evaluate the model's performance, we utilized a real-world dataset comprising smart meter readings from 1,000 households. Experimental results demonstrate that our approach achieves superior effectiveness compared to existing state-of-the-art techniques.

This study examines the characteristics of sparse, -planar surface graphs that maintain a fixed number of edges per vertex. Specifically, it establishes the existence and defines the structural rules for "tight surface graphs" on the torus, Klein bottle, and projective plane. By applying these definitions, the paper derives various significant consequences.

The LHCb experiment has determined the lifetime of the $\mathcal{\Omega}^0_c$ baryon by analyzing its decay into $K^0_{\rm S}K^+\pi^-$ final states, utilizing an integrated luminosity of $3.0\, \mathrm{fb}^{-1}$ from proton-proton collisions at a center-of-mass energy of $7\, \mathrm{TeV}$. The measured lifetime is $\tau(\mathcal{\Omega}^0_c) = (292 \pm 14 \, (\text{stat}) \pm 15 \, (\text{sys}))\, \mathrm{ps}$. This result aligns with prior LHCb measurements of the $\Lambda^0_b$ and $\mathcal{\Omega}^0_c$ lifetimes, supporting the hypothesis that lifetimes for baryons containing the same heavy quark are roughly equivalent.

Subspace clustering has become a prominent unsupervised learning technique in remote sensing, offering significant advantages over traditional methods like K-means and hierarchical clustering. This survey examines various subspace clustering approaches tailored for unsupervised remote sensing tasks. Initially, it outlines fundamental concepts of subspace clustering, including key algorithms and evaluation metrics. Next, it reviews diverse methods used to construct data matrices and feature representations, which are critical for achieving effective subspace clustering. Finally, the paper presents results from major remote sensing datasets to assess and compare the efficacy of these different subspace methods.

This study introduces a new method for estimating the thermal conductivity and albedo of Arctic sea ice, utilizing a dataset of 1,000 temperature profiles collected from 1979 to 1992. The approach employs a non-linear least squares optimization technique to minimize the discrepancy between observed temperature data and a model based on the 1-D heat diffusion equation. The model incorporates spatially variable albedo and thermal conductivity, as well as an internal heat source representing absorbed solar radiation. The analysis reveals that the estimated albedo and conductivity values exhibit a strong dependency on the specific choice of the heat source function. Furthermore, the robustness of the inversion process is evaluated by testing it against synthetic data sets.

We demonstrate that dynamic magnetic fields can induce a Fano-type interference effect in ultracold atom-molecule scattering, enabling the isolation of specific final states. This mechanism involves a two-level system where the scattering channel interferes with a defect state induced by a magnetic field. By adjusting the field's frequency, we can precisely control the scattering cross-section, effectively acting as a tunable filter for final states. This approach offers a promising method for generating samples with a controlled composition of ultracold atoms and molecules.

This study proposes a novel class of nonextensive thermostatistics that extends Tsallis statistics, driven by the observation that non-extensive systems often exhibit complex dynamics, such as chaotic behavior. We introduce a nonadditive entropy formulation that accounts for these irregularities and derive its corresponding composition rule. Subsequently, we apply this theory to formulate a generalized maximum entropy principle, resulting in a generalized central limit theorem. This theorem quantifies the fluctuations of non-additive entropies within non-extensive systems, demonstrating that such fluctuations can be substantial. Finally, we illustrate the applicability of this framework using a non-extensive generalization of the Ornstein-Uhlenbeck process, showing how it captures the temporal evolution of non-extensive variables.

This study explores the emergence of Floquet Weyl semimetal states within a periodically driven, three-dimensional topological insulator. We demonstrate that by applying time-reversal symmetry-breaking periodic modulation, one can induce the conversion of trivial bulk bands into Floquet Weyl bands, thereby creating Floquet Weyl nodes. Furthermore, our analysis reveals that these states exhibit an anomalous surface state characterized by Fermi arc-like arcs, confirming their nature as topological semimetals. Additionally, we identify the presence of Floquet Weyl points situated on the surface, which serve as termination points for these Fermi arcs.

Decentralized computing protocols, such as those built on blockchain, are designed to incentivize independent actors to perform accurate calculations. This paper introduces a new protocol, Decentralized Federated Learning (DecFed), which utilizes blockchain to decentralize the training of machine learning models. In this framework, participants are rewarded for contributing data and model parameters during the training process, while those who attempt to deceive are penalized. This study demonstrates that DecFed successfully incentivizes the acquisition of a model with statistical utility equivalent to that of centralized federated learning. Furthermore, we evaluate the protocol's performance using a case study on a real-world dataset, highlighting the critical role of transaction fees in its execution.

The primary challenge in optimizing rate-distortion for 3D point clouds lies in the high computational cost associated with distortion calculations. To address this, we introduce a novel prediction strategy that leverages the geometric attributes of point clouds. Specifically, we utilize the spatial proximity of points to forecast the color of a target pixel based on its neighbors. This approach significantly reduces distortion calculations by limiting the prediction to a small set of nearby points. Furthermore, we employ a dynamic pruning mechanism to filter out irrelevant neighboring points, thereby enhancing prediction efficiency. Experimental results demonstrate that our method achieves superior compression performance compared to current state-of-the-art techniques.

We investigate the QCD phase diagram at finite temperature and chemical potential using the chiral random matrix model, which incorporates the $U(1)$-$U_A$ symmetry anomaly. Our results demonstrate that the critical lines for chiral symmetry breaking and deconfinement nearly overlap, a finding that aligns with the Roberge-Weiss periodicity observed in the QCD phase diagram.

The scarcity of ground truth annotations in medical imaging is a primary barrier to the widespread adoption of deep learning. Self-supervised learning (SSL) offers a solution by enabling the training of deep models without labeled data. This study introduces a self-supervised framework for segmenting brain tumors in MRI scans, utilizing a contrastive learning approach to derive feature representations from unlabeled data. These features are then fine-tuned on a small set of labeled data to perform segmentation. Experiments were conducted on the BraTS 2019 dataset, comparing the proposed method against state-of-the-art supervised and self-supervised models. Results indicate that the method achieves performance comparable to supervised learning, with the added benefit of eliminating the need for extensive annotated datasets.

Font creation is notoriously laborious, demanding extensive manual labor and domain expertise. In contrast, few-shot font generation offers a promising alternative by deriving character glyphs from minimal examples, drastically reducing the need for intricate design skills. Although recent advancements in this field have shown success, they often rely on specific datasets or architectures, limiting their practical utility. To address this, we introduce a novel few-shot font generation framework designed for rapid deployment on various character glyph datasets. Our approach utilizes a dual-stream Transformer encoder-decoder system, where the encoder captures the semantic essence of character images and the decoder reconstructs them. To ensure the generated fonts maintain consistency across different characters, we employ a novel positional encoding scheme. Furthermore, to enhance the quality of output, we incorporate a Q-contrastive loss function that strengthens the model's ability to distinguish between glyph classes. Experimental results on the FontVerse benchmark demonstrate that our method outperforms existing state-of-the-art techniques.

This study examines the interaction between a charged fluid and spacetime torsion within the context of Arnowitt-Deser-Misner (ADM) formalism. We analyze the induced effects stemming from this coupling in stationary spacetime backgrounds, specifically focusing on how it alters the horizon properties of charged black holes. Furthermore, we derive a generalized first law of black hole thermodynamics that incorporates both fluid dynamics and torsion contributions.

This paper introduces a digital twin-assisted adaptive video streaming framework designed to enhance user experience. By leveraging digital twins, the system anticipates future network conditions to proactively adjust video quality, thereby mitigating buffering delays. To further refine performance, we develop a user-specific model that predicts the relationship between network states and throughput, enabling the twin to forecast throughput based on future network predictions. This model is continuously refined using online learning techniques. Additionally, we employ a reinforcement learning approach to determine optimal video selection strategies given predicted future networks. Simulation outcomes demonstrate that our proposed method achieves superior performance compared to existing solutions.

Neutrino astronomy has recently entered a new era, marked by the detection of astrophysical neutrinos by IceCube. These events are anticipated to reveal flavor ratios of $1:1:1$ upon reaching Earth, a signature resulting from oscillations within the ultra-high-energy neutrinos produced at their source. This study presents a theoretical analysis of flavor ratios for astrophysical neutrinos across the GeV to TeV range, incorporating both intrinsic production mechanisms and subsequent propagation effects. We demonstrate that, despite diverse assumptions regarding the composition of astrophysical sources, neutrino oscillations consistently yield a flavor ratio of $1:1:1$ at Earth. These ratios are expected to be observable by upcoming detectors such as KM3NeT and ANTARES. Furthermore, our results indicate that astrophysical neutrinos in the sub-TeV to TeV spectrum could serve as a valuable tool for investigating the origins of these neutrinos and characterizing their generation processes.
